But to virtuous men it is added there straightway: [[Rom 8:9|you are not in the flesh, but the spirit, if so be that the Spirit|Vos in carne non estis, sed in spiritu]]. The rest is expounded as has been said.

paras.t: Vult itaque princeps Apostolorum asserere quod Christus, qui nostris temporibus carne indutus, veniens prædicavit hominibus iter salutis, ipse etiam et ante diluvium eis qui tunc increduli erant, spiritu veniens prædicavit. Ipse namque per Spiritum Sanctum erat in Noe et in aliis Sanctis qui tunc erant, per quos tunc prædicavit iniquis illius temporis, ut converterentur. Sicque beatissimus Petrus in verbis istis apertissime innuit Christi divinitatem, et utriusque naturæ unam esse personam in ipso. Quamvis enim tunc nondum fuerit incarnatus, tamen vere tunc, imo et æternaliter fuit et est, quia suppositum est æternum. Et Christus supponit personam æternam et increatam. Propter quod ait in Joanne: Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum. Ad quod insinuandum, Judas apostolus in sua ait Canonica: Jesus populum salvans de terra Ægypti, secundo eos qui non crediderunt, perdidit. Ad Hebræos quoque fertur: Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula.
paras.en: So the prince of the Apostles means to assert that Christ, who in our times, clothed in flesh, came and preached to men the way of salvation, himself also before the flood, coming in spirit, preached to those who were then unbelieving. For he was through the Holy Ghost in Noe and in the other Saints who then lived, through whom he then preached to the wicked of that time, that they might be converted. And so the most blessed Peter in these words most plainly intimates the divinity of Christ, and that there is one person of both natures in him. For although he was not then yet incarnate, yet he truly was then, nay was and is eternally, because the suppositum is eternal [that is, the individual subject, the Person of the Word]. And *Christ* stands for an eternal and uncreated person. Wherefore he says in John: [[John 8:58|before Abraham was made, I AM|Antequam Abraham fieret, ego sum]]. To intimate this, Jude the apostle says in his Canonical Epistle: [[Jude 1:5|Jesus, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, did afterwards destroy them that believed not|Jesus populum salvans de terra Ægypti, secundo eos qui non crediderunt, perdidit]]. To the Hebrews also it is said: [[Heb 13:8|Jesus Christ, yesterday, and today: and the same for ever|Jesus Christus heri et hodie, ipse et in sæcula]].

paras.t: Insuper quidam per carcerem intelligunt limbum patrum, ut sit sensus: In quo, ut scilicet plures Deo offerret ipse Christus, veniens spiritu, id est secundum animam suam, in carcerem, id est in limbum ubi sancti patres detinebantur (in quem Christus, ut spiritum tradidit, secundum animam mox descendit); prædicavit his qui detinebantur ibidem, id est, mysterium suæ incarnationis et passionis impletum esse annuntiavit: qui increduli fuerant aliquando, quando exspectabat Dei patientia in diebus Noe, quum fabricaretur arca, etc.: quia (ut pie speratur) quidam qui ante diluvium increduli erant verbis Noe, veniente ipso diluvio, suæ perfidiæ cognoverunt errorem, et pœnituerunt ac salvabantur, ita quod in purgatorio plene purgati, venerunt in limbum patrum, sicque eis cum ceteris ibi manentibus Christus, ut dictum est, prædicavit.
paras.en: Moreover, some understand by the prison the limbo of the fathers, so that the sense is: In which, namely that he might offer more to God, Christ himself, coming in spirit, that is, according to his soul, into the prison, that is, into limbo where the holy fathers were detained (into which Christ, as soon as he gave up the ghost, at once descended according to his soul), preached to those who were held there, that is, announced that the mystery of his incarnation and passion was fulfilled: [[3:20|Which had been some time incredulous, when they waited for the patience of God in the days of Noe, when the ark was a building|qui increduli fuerant aliquando, quando exspectabat Dei patientia in diebus Noe, quum fabricaretur arca]], etc.: because (as is piously hoped) some who before the flood were unbelieving at the words of Noe, when the flood itself came, recognized the error of their unbelief, and repented and were saved, so that, fully purged in purgatory, they came into the limbo of the fathers; and so to them, with the others remaining there, Christ preached, as has been said.

paras.t: — Quidam vero incaute, imo et insipienter dixerunt, quod Christus in infernum descendens, prædicavit ibi detentis pœnitentiam et viam salutis, seque mundi salvatorem consistere, et quod tunc credentes in eum salvabantur: inter quos quidam dixerunt Platonem fuisse primum credentium. Istud inter apocryphorum computandum est somnium. Et S. Cyrillus atque Chrysostomus huic contradicunt assertioni. Tempus quippe et status merendi ac demerendi, finem accipiunt in cujuslibet hominis morte. Propter quod asserit Damascenus: Quod angelis est ruina, hoc hominibus est mors. Et in Ecclesiaste legitur: Si ceciderit lignum ad austrum aut ad aquilonem, in quocumque loco ceciderit, ibi erit. Idcirco de lege communi post vitam præsentem non est reditus ad pœnitentiam salutarem. Sed Deus omni lege sublimior est; et quibusdam, ut vult, privilegium facit.
paras.en: — But some have said incautiously, nay even foolishly, that Christ descending into hell preached to those held there repentance and the way of salvation, and that he was the Saviour of the world, and that those who then believed in him were saved: among whom some said that Plato was the first of the believers. This must be counted among the dreams of the apocrypha. And St. Cyril and Chrysostom contradict this assertion. For the time and state of meriting and demeriting come to an end at the death of every man. Wherefore Damascene asserts: What the fall is to the angels, that death is to men. And in Ecclesiastes we read: [[Eccles 11:3|If the tree fall to the south, or to the north, in what place soever it shall fall, there shall it be|Si ceciderit lignum ad austrum aut ad aquilonem, in quocumque loco ceciderit, ibi erit]]. Therefore by the common law there is no return to saving repentance after the present life. But God is higher than every law, and grants a privilege to some as he wills.

paras.t: In qua arca pauci, id est octo animæ, sumendo partem pro toto, id est octo homines, utpote Noe et uxor ipsius, tres quoque filii Noe, et tres eorum uxores, salvæ factæ sunt, id est a periculo diluvii, scilicet submersione et morte, per aquam, id est per hoc quod aqua diluvii elevavit arcam in altum, ne mergerentur. Sumitur autem in Scripturis multoties pars pro toto: sicut in Psalmo, Ad te omnis caro veniet; et in Actibus, Eramus omnes animæ in navi ducentæ septuaginta sex.
paras.en: [[3:20|wherein a few, that is, eight souls|In qua arca pauci, id est octo animæ]] — in which ark — taking the part for the whole, that is, eight persons, namely Noe and his wife, and the three sons of Noe and their three wives[[Gen 6:18||]][[Gen 7:7||]][[Gen 8:18||]], [[3:20|were saved|salvæ factæ sunt]], that is, from the peril of the flood, namely drowning and death, [[3:20|by water|per aquam]], that is, by this, that the water of the flood lifted the ark on high, so that they were not sunk. Now in the Scriptures the part is often taken for the whole: as in the Psalm, [[Ps 64:3|all flesh shall come to thee|Ad te omnis caro veniet]]; and in the Acts, [[Acts 27:37|we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls|Eramus omnes animæ in navi ducentæ septuaginta sex]].

paras.t: (Quod et vos nunc similis formæ salvos facit Baptisma. Ordo verborum in constructione hic est: Quod (supple, dico quia) Baptisma similis formæ, id est sacramentum Baptismatis Christi existens similis formæ, id est comparis modi cum aquis diluvii. Nam, sicut per aquam diluvii salvi facti sunt valde pauci, comparatione eorum qui perierunt diluvio; ita electi qui per Baptismum salvantur, perpauci sunt, comparatione fidelium reproborum et aliorum incredulorum. Propterea ait Salvator: Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam, et pauci inveniunt eam; et rursus, Nolite (inquit) timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Rursus, sicut aqua diluvii elevando arcam, salvavit exsistentes in ea, sic aqua Baptismi salvat, levando ad cœlum. Itaque, Baptisma similis formæ salvos vos facit, id est, purgat a vitiis atque ad alia sacramenta deducit. Est enim primum inter sacramenta, et janua ad alia. Non carnis depositio sordium, id est, corporalium fœditatum seu immunditiarum depositio non vos salvat, sed spiritualis interiorque ablutio. Ideo subditur: sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum, id est interrogatio quæ fit a baptizando adulto: interrogatio, inquam, bonæ conscientiæ in Deum, id est inquisitio an habeat conscientiam bonam in Deo, ita ut non fictus accedat, sed catholice credens, et boni propositi. Hæc interrogatio salvat, id est, per eam fit baptizandi salvatio. Aliter enim non consequitur quis Baptismi effectum, si adultus exsistat. Tunc enim ab ipso fit interrogatio, personaliterque respondet. Si autem sit infans, patrinus respondet pro eo. Per resurrectionem Jesu Christi, id est, an habeat conscientiam bonam in Deo per resurrectionem Jesu Christi, id est per vivam et formatam fidem resurrectionis Jesu Christi, recte credendo in eum. Qui enim credit Christum resurrexisse a mortuis, alia ejus mysteria facilius credere potest. Sicque resurrectio Christi valde specialem habet difficultatem credendi. Ideo scriptum est in Actibus: Virtute magna reddebant Apostoli testimonium resurrectionis Jesu Christi Domini nostri.
paras.en: [[3:21|Whereunto baptism, being of the like form, now saveth you also|Quod et vos nunc similis formæ salvos facit Baptisma]]. The order of the words in construction is this: *Whereunto* (supply: I say because) *baptism of like form*, that is, the sacrament of Christ's Baptism, being of like form, that is, of a manner comparable with the waters of the flood. For as through the water of the flood very few were saved, in comparison with those who perished in the flood, so the elect who are saved through Baptism are very few in comparison with the reprobate among the faithful and the other unbelievers. Therefore the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:14|strait is the way that leadeth to life: and few there are that find it!|Arcta est via quæ ducit ad vitam, et pauci inveniunt eam]] and again: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite … timere … dare vobis regnum]]. Again, as the water of the flood, by lifting the ark, saved those in it, so the water of Baptism saves by lifting to heaven. So baptism of like form *saveth you*, that is, cleanses from vices and leads to the other sacraments; for it is the first among the sacraments and the door to the others. [[3:21|not the putting away of the filth of the flesh|Non carnis depositio sordium]], that is, the putting away of bodily foulness or uncleanness does not save you, but a spiritual and inward washing. Therefore it is added: [[3:21|but, the examination of a good conscience towards God|sed conscientiæ bonæ interrogatio in Deum]], that is, the questioning made of the adult to be baptized: the questioning, I say, of a good conscience towards God, that is, the inquiry whether he has a good conscience in God, so that he comes not feignedly but believing as a Catholic and of good purpose. This questioning saves, that is, through it the salvation of the one baptized comes about. For otherwise one does not obtain the effect of Baptism if he be an adult. For then the questioning is made of him and he answers in person; but if he be an infant, the godfather answers for him. [[3:21|by the resurrection of Jesus Christ|Per resurrectionem Jesu Christi]], that is, whether he has a good conscience in God through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, that is, through a living and formed faith [that is, faith informed by charity] in the resurrection of Jesus Christ, believing rightly in him. For he who believes that Christ rose from the dead can more easily believe his other mysteries. And thus the resurrection of Christ has a very special difficulty of belief. Therefore it is written in the Acts: [[Acts 4:33|with great power did the Apostles give testimony of the resurrection of Jesus Christ our Lord|Virtute magna reddebant Apostoli testimonium resurrectionis Jesu Christi Domini nostri]].

paras.t: Qui est ad dexteram Dei Patris: juxta illud Marci: Dominus Jesus postquam locutus est eis, assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei. Dicitur autem Christus ad Dei dexteram esse, dupliciter: primo, in quantum est Deus, sedet et regnat Deo Patri æqualis; sed in quantum homo, dicitur ad Patris dexteram residere, id est in potioribus ejus bonis consistere, quia præ universis electis fruitur Deitate sublimiter, et omni felicitate impletus est, quantum capere potest natura creata. Deglutiens mortem: quia in primis sua benedicta passione sibi ipsi plenam corporis immortalitatem promeruit, deinde genus humanum a morte culpæ redemit, imo et a morte æternæ damnationis salvavit. Plenam quoque animæ et corporis beatitudinem, quæ omnem mortalitatem excludit, promeruit nobis: quam virtute et merito Christi tandem sortientur electi, puta in die judicii, quando mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem, et juxta quod loquitur Paulus, implebitur sermo qui scriptus est: Absorpta est mors in victoria. Hinc subditur: ut vitæ æternæ heredes efficeremur, id est, æternam salutem hereditate consequeremur. Unde per Osee prophetam ait Salvator: De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos: ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne.
paras.en: [[3:22|Who is on the right hand of God|Qui est ad dexteram Dei]] the Father: according to that of Mark: [[Mark 16:19|the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sitteth on the right hand of God|Dominus Jesus postquam locutus est eis, assumptus est in cœlum, et sedet a dextris Dei]]. Now Christ is said to be at God's right hand in two ways: first, inasmuch as he is God, he sits and reigns equal to God the Father; but inasmuch as he is man, he is said to sit at the Father's right hand, that is, to abide in his greater goods, because above all the elect he enjoys the Deity sublimely, and is filled with all felicity, as far as created nature can receive. [[3:22|swallowing down death|Deglutiens mortem]]: because first by his blessed passion he merited for himself full immortality of body, then redeemed mankind from the death of guilt, nay saved it from the death of eternal damnation. He merited for us also the full beatitude of soul and body, which excludes all mortality: which by the power and merit of Christ the elect will at length obtain, namely at the day of judgment, when [[1 Cor 15:53|this mortal must put on immortality|mortale hoc induerit immortalitatem]], and, as Paul says, [[1 Cor 15:54|the saying that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory|implebitur sermo qui scriptus est: Absorpta est mors in victoria]]. Hence it is added: [[3:22|that we might be made heirs of life everlasting|ut vitæ æternæ heredes efficeremur]], that is, that we might obtain eternal salvation as an inheritance. Hence through Osee the prophet the Saviour says: [[Osee 13:14|I will deliver them out of the hand of death. I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy death; O hell, I will be thy bite|De manu mortis liberabo eos, de morte redimam eos: ero mors tua, o mors; morsus tuus ero, inferne]].

paras.t: Profectus in cœlum in die ascensionis. Per quod nobis dedit fiduciam præbuitque exemplum beatificæ ascensionis in cœlum cum corpore glorificato et anima, obtinendæ in die judicii, quando dicet: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum, etc. Subjectis sibi angelis, et potestatibus, et virtutibus: quia super omnium angelicorum ordinum dignitatem, hierarchiam et excellentiam, elevatus est Christus in ascensione, secundum naturam assumptam. Quocirca sciendum, quod eo ipso quo Christi humanitas, in incarnatione Verbi æterni, unita est Verbo hypostatica unione, videlicet ad personale et increatum esse Verbi assumpta in unitate personæ, prælata est omni creaturæ, et toto universo dignior sublimiorque effecta. Tamen in quantum mortalitati et passibilitati fuit subjecta, erat quodammodo angelis sanctis inferior. Sed quia ad immortalem vitam surrexit, et super omnes cœlos usque ad dexteram Patris ascendit, idcirco in ascensione dicuntur angeli et ceteri chori cœlestes, ei subjecti.
paras.en: [[3:22|being gone into heaven|Profectus in cœlum]] on the day of the ascension. By which he gave us confidence and offered an example of the beatifying ascension into heaven with glorified body and soul, to be obtained at the day of judgment, when he shall say: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum]], etc. [[3:22|the angels and powers and virtues being made subject to him|Subjectis sibi angelis, et potestatibus, et virtutibus]]: because above the dignity, hierarchy and excellence of all the angelic orders Christ was raised in the ascension, according to the nature assumed. Wherefore it must be known that by the very fact that Christ's humanity, in the incarnation of the eternal Word, was united to the Word by hypostatic union [that is, union in the one Person], namely assumed to the personal and uncreated being of the Word in unity of person, it was set above every creature and made worthier and more sublime than the whole universe. Yet inasmuch as it was subject to mortality and passibility, it was in a certain manner lower than the holy angels. But because he rose to immortal life and ascended above all the heavens even to the Father's right hand, therefore in the ascension the angels and the other heavenly choirs are said to be subject to him.

paras.t: Et exprimuntur hic tres chori angelici, seu tres ordines angelorum, per quos ceteri dantur intelligi. Quocirca pensandum, quod gloriosissimus apostolici agminis vertex, paulatim ascendendo, primo exprimit Angelos, deinde Potestates, et tertio loco Virtutes. Ex quo sumitur argumentum, quod Virtutes pertineant ad secundam hierarchiam angelicam, et supra Potestates exsistant, prout divinus Dionysius a Paulo apostolo informatus, edocuit: quamquam Gregorius et Bernardus ponant Virtutes in infima hierarchia chorum supremum.
paras.en: And three angelic choirs, or three orders of angels, are named here, by which the others are given to be understood. Wherefore it is to be weighed that the most glorious head of the apostolic band, ascending step by step, names first the Angels, then the Powers, and in the third place the Virtues. From which an argument is drawn that the Virtues belong to the second angelic hierarchy and stand above the Powers, as the divine Dionysius, instructed by the apostle Paul, taught: although Gregory and Bernard place the Virtues as the highest choir in the lowest hierarchy.

4.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI QUARTI : CHRISTO IGITUR PASSO IN CARNE.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Christ therefore having suffered in the flesh.

paras.t: Quum in imitatione conversationis passionisque Christi tota nostra consistat perfectio, ubertim princeps Apostolorum ad dominicæ passionis imitationem nos admonet, per adversitatum et tribulationum tolerantiam virtuosam. Idcirco nunc loquitur:
paras.en: Since our whole perfection consists in the imitation of Christ's manner of life and of His passion, the prince of the Apostles admonishes us abundantly to imitate the Lord's passion through the virtuous endurance of adversities and tribulations. Therefore he now says:

paras.t: Christo igitur passo in carne, id est, quia Christus in carne propria passus est, non in deitate sua, quæ fuit impassibilis prorsus. Nec solum in carne sua patiebatur Salvator, sed in anima quoque. Habuitque corporales et spirituales, exteriores et interiores dolores, ita quod in omnibus exterioribus et interioribus suis sensibus affligebatur, atque in appetitu sensitivo tam concupiscibili quam irascibili. Nam et timorem et tristitiam habuit. Cœpit quippe contristari, et pavere, et tædere, dixitque: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem. Nec solum in prædictis organicis viribus, sed in potentiis quoque superioribus intellectivis graviter patiebatur, videlicet intellectu et voluntate. Quamvis enim anima ejus, quantum ad superiores has vires, fuerat tempore passionis in gaudio beatificæ fruitionis, ita quod non patiebatur in potentiis illis ad increatum objectum relatis, tamen in quantum potentiæ illæ erant fundatæ in essentia animæ, et respectum habebant ad objectum creatum afflictivum, sic erant in grandi afflictione, prout Thomas in tertia parte Summæ suæ hæc plenius docet. Imo, ut Bonaventura et alii bene deducunt, in Christo tempore passionis dolor compassionis excessit passionis dolorem. Sicque tota Christi humanitas vehementissime patiebatur, et tota natura humana in ipso, fuit in dolore summo ac maximo, quia tenerrimæ erat complexionis et summe perceptiva doloris, et erat maxime recens, vivax, nobilis, ac robusta. Nec fuit tunc in ea a superioribus viribus in inferiores redundantia consolatoria, doloris relevativa. Merito igitur debemus compati Christo, tantum et tanta propter nos passo, et ejus passioni nos conformare. Propter quod subditur:
paras.en: [[4:1|Christ therefore having suffered in the flesh|Christo igitur passo in carne]]: that is, because Christ suffered in His own flesh, not in His deity, which was altogether impassible. Nor did the Saviour suffer in His flesh only, but in His soul also. He had pains of body and of spirit, outward and inward, so that He was afflicted in all His outward and inward senses, and in the sensitive appetite, the concupiscible as well as the irascible [that is, the appetite that desires what is pleasant and the appetite that rises against what is hard or hostile]. For He had both fear and sadness. For He [[Matt 26:37|began to grow sorrowful|Cœpit quippe contristari]], and to fear, and to be heavy[[Mark 14:33||]], and said: [[Matt 26:38|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]][[Mark 14:34||]]. And not only in the aforesaid organic powers [that is, the powers that act through a bodily organ], but in the higher, intellective powers also, namely the intellect and the will, He suffered grievously. For although His soul, as to these higher powers, was at the time of the passion in the joy of the beatific fruition, so that He did not suffer in those powers as they are directed to their uncreated object, yet in so far as those powers were grounded in the essence of the soul, and had regard to a created object that afflicted them, they were in great affliction, as Thomas teaches this more fully in the third part of his Summa. Indeed, as Bonaventure and others rightly argue, in Christ at the time of the passion the pain of compassion exceeded the pain of the passion. And so the whole humanity of Christ suffered most vehemently, and the whole human nature in Him was in the highest and greatest pain, because it was of the most tender complexion and most keenly sensitive to pain, and was utterly fresh, vigorous, noble and robust. Nor was there then in it any overflow of consolation from the higher powers into the lower to relieve the pain. Rightly therefore ought we to suffer with Christ, who suffered so much and such things for us, and to conform ourselves to His passion. Therefore it is added:

paras.t: Et vos eadem cogitatione armamini, id est, meditatione dominicæ passionis armate vos contra impugnationem deliciarum, seu concupiscentiarum, et vitiorum, et clypeo pœnitentiæ vos munite, passionemque Christi sequi proponite, carnem vestram cum vitiis et concupiscentiis crucifigendo.
paras.en: [[4:1|be you also armed with the same thought|Et vos eadem cogitatione armamini]]: that is, arm yourselves with meditation on the Lord's passion against the assault of pleasures, or concupiscences, and of vices, and fortify yourselves with the shield of penance, and resolve to follow the passion of Christ, crucifying your flesh with its vices and concupiscences[[Gal 5:24||]].

paras.t: Quia qui passus est in carne, desiit a peccatis. Si Desinere, accipiatur pro Cessare ab actu præterito seu incepto, certum est istud de Christo non posse exponi, eo quod nunquam peccaverit. Si autem Desinere, accipiatur pro Abstinere, potest de Christo intelligi. Nam ipse Christus in carne propter nos passus, abstinuit semper a culpis. Communiter vero exponitur istud de imitatoribus dominicæ passionis, ut sit sensus: Quia qui passus est in carne, id est, tribulationes corporales patienter sustinuit, et carnem suam affligendo per abstinentias, jejunia, disciplinas, vigilias, eam in animæ servitutem redegit, juxta illud: Castigo corpus meum, et in servitutem redigo; desiit a peccatis, id est, a præteritis vitiis pœnituit, et se emendavit, nec carnalibus inquinamentis se fœdat. Unde Sponsa in Canticis: Lavi, inquit, pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo illos?
paras.en: [[4:1|for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sins|Quia qui passus est in carne, desiit a peccatis]]. If *to cease* is taken for leaving off an act that is past or begun, it is certain that this cannot be explained of Christ, since He never sinned. But if *to cease* is taken for *to abstain*, it can be understood of Christ. For Christ Himself, having suffered in the flesh for us, always abstained from faults. Commonly, however, this is explained of the imitators of the Lord's passion, so that the sense is: [[4:1|for he that hath suffered in the flesh|Quia qui passus est in carne]], that is, has patiently borne bodily tribulations, and, afflicting his flesh by abstinences, fasts, disciplines [that is, scourgings taken as penance] and vigils, has brought it into subjection to the soul, according to that saying: [[1 Cor 9:27|I chastise my body and bring it into subjection|Castigo corpus meum, et in servitutem redigo]]; [[4:1|hath ceased from sins|desiit a peccatis]], that is, has repented of his past vices and amended himself, and does not defile himself with carnal uncleanness. Hence the Bride in the Canticle: [[Cant 5:3|I have washed|Lavi]], she says, [[Cant 5:3|my feet, how shall I defile them?|pedes meos, quomodo inquinabo illos?]]

paras.t: Ut jam non hominum desideriis, id est de cetero non carnalibus et humanis inordinatis affectibus, sed voluntati Dei, id est observationi divinorum præceptorum ad gloriam Creatoris, quod reliquum est in carne vivat temporis, id est, residuum temporis vitæ præsentis in hac carne mortali vivat et obediat, hoc est, vos ipsi de cetero per omne tempus vitæ vestræ serviatis obediatisque Deo. Tempus quippe dicitur agere vel pati, quod exsistentes in tempore agunt aut patiuntur, sicut in Evangelio ait Salvator: Crastinus dies sibi ipsi erit sollicitus. Et in primo libro Machabæorum habetur: Videns Jonathas quia tempus eum juvat.
paras.en: [[4:2|That now|Ut jam]] [[4:2|not after the desires of men|non hominum desideriis]], that is, henceforth not after carnal and human disordered affections, [[4:2|but according to the will of God|sed voluntati Dei]], that is, according to the keeping of the divine commandments for the glory of the Creator, [[4:2|he may live the rest of his time in the flesh|quod reliquum est in carne vivat temporis]]: that is, that the rest of the time of the present life may live in this mortal flesh and obey; that is, that you yourselves henceforth, for all the time of your life, may serve and obey God. For time is said to do or to suffer what those who exist in time do or suffer, as the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 6:34|the morrow will be solicitous for itself|Crastinus dies sibi ipsi erit sollicitus]]. And in the first book of Machabees we have: [[1 Mach 12:1|Jonathan saw that the time served him|Videns Jonathas quia tempus eum juvat]].

paras.t: Sufficit enim præteritum tempus ad voluntatem gentium consummandam, id est, satis et plus quam satis est quod elapsis temporibus vixistis carnaliter, et irrationabilium hominum voluntatibus acquievistis. Idcirco de reliquo, non solum a consuetis peccatis cessetis, sed præteritorum quoque temporum negligentias recuperetis, et vitia deploretis, semperque fructuose vivatis. Qui ambulaverunt ad infernum, in luxuriis, desideriis irrefrenatis, vinolentiis, id est assiduis et superfluis vini potationibus, quæ non solum animæ, sed et corpori maxime nocent (quibus dicitur apud Isaiam: Væ qui consurgitis mane ad ebrietatem sectandam, et potandum usque ad vesperam), comessationibus, potationibus, quantum ad aliorum poculorum sumptionem immoderatam, et illicitis idolorum cultibus, idololatriis maxime vitiosis. Hæc namque et consimilia scelera in gentibus regnaverunt, prout in libro Sapientiæ diffuse conscriptum est, ubi inter cetera fertur: Omnia commixta sunt, sanguis, homicidium, furtum et fictio, corruptio, infidelitas, turbatio, perjurium, tumultus, bonorum Domini immemoratio, animarum inquinatio, inordinatio mœchiæ et impudicitiæ.
paras.en: [[4:3|For the time past is sufficient to have fulfilled the will of the Gentiles|Sufficit enim præteritum tempus ad voluntatem gentium consummandam]]: that is, it is enough and more than enough that in times gone by you lived carnally and gave in to the wills of unreasoning men. Therefore for the rest of your time, not only cease from your accustomed sins, but also make up for the negligences of past times, and bewail your vices, and live always fruitfully. [[4:3|who have walked|Qui ambulaverunt]] to hell, [[4:3|in riotousness, lusts|in luxuriis, desideriis]] unbridled, [[4:3|excess of wine|vinolentiis]], that is, constant and excessive drinkings of wine, which are most harmful not only to the soul but to the body also (to such it is said in Isaias: [[Is 5:11|Woe to you that rise up early in the morning to follow drunkenness, and to drink in the evening|Væ qui consurgitis mane ad ebrietatem sectandam, et potandum usque ad vesperam]]), [[4:3|revellings, banquetings|comessationibus, potationibus]] [the Latin *potationes* is literally "drinking-bouts"], as to the immoderate taking of other drinks, [[4:3|and unlawful worshipping of idols|et illicitis idolorum cultibus]], idolatries most vicious. For these and the like crimes reigned among the Gentiles, as is written at length in the book of Wisdom, where among other things it is said: [[Wis 14:25|all things are mingled together, blood, murder, theft, and dissimulation, corruption and unfaithfulness, tumults and perjury|Omnia commixta sunt, sanguis, homicidium, furtum et fictio, corruptio, infidelitas, turbatio, perjurium]], tumult, forgetfulness of the good things of the Lord, [[Wis 14:26|defiling of souls|animarum inquinatio]], [[Wis 14:26|the irregularity of adultery and uncleanness|inordinatio mœchiæ et impudicitiæ]] [Denis's text differs here and there from the Vulgate as now printed, and leaves out some items].

paras.t: In quibus nunc admirantur, non concurrentibus vobis in eamdem luxuriæ confusionem: id est, dum vitia ista exercent, mirantur quod vos qui olim fuistis socii eorum in talibus, nunc abstrahitis vos ab eis, blasphemantes Christum et fidem quam accepistis. Non enim cognoscunt viam justitiæ, ideo justos reputant fatuos. De talibus scriptum est per Sapientem: Dixerunt impii, cogitantes non recte: Venite, fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tanquam in juventute celeriter; vino pretioso et unguentis impleamus nos; nullum pratum sit, quod non pertranseat luxuria nostra. Denique multi sunt Christiani ita carnales et excæcati, ut mirentur si quis ad vitam claustralem et pœnitentialem confugiat, et ipsorum vitet consortia. Admiratio quippe consurgit ex hoc, quod insolitus effectus conspicitur cujus causa ignoratur. Hi autem obtenebrati pravi, non sciunt nec pensant quid moveat justos, et qualiter inspirentur a Deo. Propter quod ad Corinthios habetur: Animalis homo non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei: stultitia enim est illi, et non potest intelligere.
paras.en: [[4:4|Wherein they think it strange|In quibus nunc admirantur]] [Denis reads *in quibus nunc*, "in which things now", where the Vulgate has *in quo*] [[4:4|that you run not with them into the same confusion of riotousness|non concurrentibus vobis in eamdem luxuriæ confusionem]]: that is, while they practise these vices, they wonder that you, who were once their companions in such things, now withdraw yourselves from them, [[4:4|speaking evil|blasphemantes]] of Christ and of the faith which you have received [Denis takes *blasphemantes* as blaspheming Christ and the faith; the Douay-Rheims has "speaking evil of you"]. For they do not know the way of justice; therefore they reckon the just to be fools. Of such it is written by the Wise Man: the wicked [[Wis 2:1|have said|Dixerunt]], [[Wis 2:1|reasoning with themselves, but not right|cogitantes non recte]]: [[Wis 2:6|Come, therefore, and let us enjoy the good things that are present, and let us speedily use the creatures as in youth|Venite, fruamur bonis quæ sunt, et utamur creatura tanquam in juventute celeriter]]; [[Wis 2:7|Let us fill ourselves with costly wine, and ointments|vino pretioso et unguentis impleamus nos]]; [[Wis 2:8|let no meadow escape our riot|nullum pratum sit, quod non pertranseat luxuria nostra]]. Lastly, there are many Christians so carnal and blinded that they wonder if anyone flees to the cloistered and penitential life and shuns their company. For wonder arises from this, that an unaccustomed effect is seen whose cause is not known. But these depraved men, darkened as they are, neither know nor consider what moves the just, and how they are inspired by God. Therefore it is said to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 2:14|the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God. For it is foolishness to him: and he cannot understand|Animalis homo non percipit ea quæ sunt Spiritus Dei: stultitia enim est illi, et non potest intelligere]].

paras.t: Qui reddent, id est, reddere exigentur, rationem ei qui paratus est judicare vivos et mortuos, utpote Christo, de quo scriptum est: Ipse est qui constitutus est a Deo judex vivorum et mortuorum. Siquidem Pater omne judicium dedit Filio. Salomon quoque protestatur: Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum.
paras.en: [[4:5|Who shall render|Qui reddent]], that is, shall be required to render, [[4:5|account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead|rationem ei qui paratus est judicare vivos et mortuos]], namely to Christ, of whom it is written: [[Acts 10:42|it is he who was appointed by God to be judge of the living and of the dead|Ipse est qui constitutus est a Deo judex vivorum et mortuorum]]. For the Father [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment to the Son|omne judicium dedit Filio]]. Solomon also solemnly declares: [[Eccles 12:14|all things that are done, God will bring into judgment for every error, whether it be good or evil|Cuncta quæ fiunt, adducet Deus in judicium pro omni errato, sive bonum sit, sive malum]].

paras.t: Propter hoc enim et mortuis evangelizatum est, id est, exsistentibus in peccatis et perfidiis prædicata est lex Christi ab ejus discipulis. De taliter mortuis ait in Evangelio Christus: Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos. Et Paulus: Vidua, inquit, quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est; et rursus, Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis. Ut judicentur quidem secundum homines in carne, id est, ipsi mortui seu iniqui jam ad Christum conversi, et impiorum consortia devitantes, dijudicentur et reprobentur ab ipsis carnalibus et excæcatis hominibus, secundum hominum hujus sæculi sensum judicantibus, quorum judicia sunt perversa. Ista tamen dijudicatio conversorum ab impiis, est præter intentionem prædicantium, et ex eorum prædicatione occasionaliter sequitur. Sicque quod ait, Ut, tenetur concomitanter, non causaliter, sicut in Psalmo: Tibi soli peccavi, etc., ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis, etc. Vivant autem secundum Deum, id est in observantia præceptorum, in spiritu, id est recta mentis intentione et ex caritatis affectione: ad quod prædicatio directe ordinabatur. Unde ad Galatas fertur: Spiritu ambulate, et desideria carnis non perficietis.
paras.en: [[4:6|For, for this cause was the gospel preached also to the dead|Propter hoc enim et mortuis evangelizatum est]]: that is, the law of Christ was preached by His disciples to those who were in sins and in unbelief. Of those dead in this way Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 8:22|let the dead bury their dead|Dimitte mortuos sepelire mortuos suos]]. And Paul: A widow, he says, that [[1 Tim 5:6|liveth in pleasures is dead while she is living|quæ in deliciis vivit, vivens mortua est]]; and again: [[Eph 5:14|Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead|Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis]]. [[4:6|That they might be judged indeed according to men, in the flesh|Ut judicentur quidem secundum homines in carne]]: that is, that these dead or wicked men, now converted to Christ and shunning the company of the ungodly, might be judged and condemned by those carnal and blinded men, who judge according to the mind of the men of this world, whose judgments are perverse. Yet this condemnation of the converted by the ungodly is beside the intention of the preachers, and follows from their preaching only as an occasion. And so the word *that* is taken as marking what goes along with it, not a cause [that is, it says what follows, not what was intended], as in the Psalm: [[Ps 50:6|To thee only have I sinned|Tibi soli peccavi]], etc., [[Ps 50:6|that thou mayst be justified in thy words|ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis]], etc. [[4:6|but may live according to God|Vivant autem secundum Deum]], that is, in the keeping of the commandments, [[4:6|in the Spirit|in spiritu]], that is, with right intention of mind and from the affection of charity: to which the preaching was directly ordered. Hence it is said to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:16|Walk in the spirit: and you shall not fulfill the lusts of the flesh|Spiritu ambulate, et desideria carnis non perficietis]].

paras.t: Et merito sic vivendum est. Omnium enim finis appropinquabit, id est, dies judicii incessabiliter appropinquat; vel, Omnium hominum finis, id est mors, indesinenter propinquat, quum tota hæc vita sit quasi cursus ad mortem.
paras.en: And rightly must we live so. [[4:7|the end of all is at hand|Omnium enim finis appropinquabit]] [Denis reads *appropinquabit*, "will draw near", where the Vulgate has *appropinquavit*]: that is, the day of judgment draws ceaselessly nearer; or, the end of all men, that is, death, draws unceasingly near, since this whole life is as it were a race towards death.

paras.t: Estote itaque prudentes, id est discreti, circumspecti et providi: quia horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis. Atque in medio laqueorum et invisibilium hostium omni ferocitate, calliditate, invidia repletorum ambulatis: qui tam fortitudine quam experientia et astutia nos valde excedunt, nec aliud machinantur nisi ut æterna felicitate, quam perdiderunt, nos spolient, infernalibusque nos secum involvant suppliciis. Idcirco oportet nos jugiter esse maxime circumspectos, timoratos, custoditos, sollicitos, prout in Deuteronomio sanctus Moyses exhortatur: Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite; ne obliviscaris verborum Domini, et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ.
paras.en: [[4:7|Be prudent therefore|Estote itaque prudentes]], that is, discerning, circumspect and provident: for [[Heb 10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God|horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis]]. And you walk in the midst of snares and of invisible enemies full of all ferocity, cunning and envy, who greatly surpass us in strength as well as in experience and craft, and who plot nothing else but to rob us of the eternal happiness which they have lost, and to entangle us with themselves in the torments of hell. Therefore we must be always most circumspect, God-fearing, guarded and watchful, as holy Moses exhorts in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]; [[Deut 4:9|Forget not the words|ne obliviscaris verborum]] of the Lord, [[Deut 4:9|and let them not go out of thy heart all the days of thy life|et ne excidant de corde tuo cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ]].

paras.t: Sed quia non sufficit diligentia nostra sine continua divinæ subventionis adsistentia, recte subjungitur: et vigilate in orationibus. Quod dupliciter potest intelligi, et debet impleri: Primo, ut orando vigilemus, id est, cum cordis vigili attentione oremus. Non enim corde hinc inde vagante invocandus est Deus, sed animo recollecto, advertente et custodito, cum omni reverentia, humilitate et sancto timore. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Ante orationem præpara animam tuam; et noli esse quasi homo tentans Deum. Secundo, ut protrahamus vigilias in orando, non solum in die, sed nocturnis quoque temporibus orationibus insistendo, juxta illud in Psalmo: Media nocte surgebam ad confitendum tibi; et rursus, In die tribulationis meæ Deum exquisivi manibus meis nocte contra eum. Hujus siquidem rei Christus (cujus omnis actio nostra est instructio) nobis dedit exemplum. De quo scriptum est: Exiit Jesus in montem solus orare, et erat pernoctans in oratione Dei. Hanc doctrinam etiam Christus expressit, apud Marcum loquens: Vigilate (nescitis enim quando Dominus veniat: sero, an media nocte, an galli cantu, an mane), ne, quum venerit repente, inveniat vos dormientes; videte, vigilate et orate.
paras.en: But since our diligence is not enough without the continual assistance of divine help, it is rightly added: [[4:7|and watch in prayers|et vigilate in orationibus]]. This can be understood, and ought to be fulfilled, in two ways. First, that we watch in praying, that is, that we pray with the watchful attention of the heart. For God is not to be called upon with a heart wandering this way and that, but with a mind recollected, attentive and guarded, with all reverence, humility and holy fear. Therefore it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 18:23|Before prayer prepare thy soul|Ante orationem præpara animam tuam]]; [[Ecclus 18:23|and be not as a man that tempteth God|et noli esse quasi homo tentans Deum]]. Secondly, that we prolong our vigils in praying, keeping on at prayer not only by day but in the night-time also, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:62|I rose at midnight to give praise to thee|Media nocte surgebam ad confitendum tibi]]; and again: [[Ps 76:3|In the days of my trouble I sought God, with my hands lifted up to him in the night|In die tribulationis meæ Deum exquisivi manibus meis nocte contra eum]]. For of this Christ (every action of whom is our instruction) gave us an example. Of Him it is written: [[Luke 6:12|he went out into a mountain to pray: and he passed the whole night in the prayer of God|Exiit Jesus in montem solus orare, et erat pernoctans in oratione Dei]] [Denis adds *Jesus* and *solus*, "alone"]. Christ also set forth this teaching, speaking in Mark: [[Mark 13:35|Watch ye|Vigilate]] ([[Mark 13:35|for you know not when the lord of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cock crowing, or in the morning|nescitis enim quando Dominus veniat: sero, an media nocte, an galli cantu, an mane]]), [[Mark 13:36|Lest coming on a sudden, he find you sleeping|ne, quum venerit repente, inveniat vos dormientes]]; [[Mark 13:33|Take ye heed, watch and pray|videte, vigilate et orate]][[Mark 13:37||]].

paras.t: Sed quoniam absque caritate nihil est meritorium, subditur: Ante omnia autem, id est potissime et in primis ante exercitia cuncta, mutuam in vobismetipsis caritatem continuam habentes, id est caritatem fraternam indesinentem, et quantum possibile est, etiam actualem, ut tam in interiores quam exteriores caritatis actus assidue procedamus, quum signum caritatis sit exsecutio actus. Unde et Dominus ait: Hoc est præceptum meum, ut diligatis invicem sicut dilexi vos. Sed quum primum maximumque præceptum sit, ut Deus toto corde ametur: quid est quod princeps Apostolorum hortatur, ut ante omnia mutuo diligamus? Et respondendum, quod eadem est caritas habitualis qua Deum proximumque diligimus, eo quod Deus sit ratio proximos diligendi. Sicque dilectio Dei et proximi se mutuo complectuntur. Idcirco, in eo quod ante omnia ad mutuam caritatem monemur, datur intelligi ut super omnia et ante omnia Deum amemus: sicque ad fraternam caritatem ante omnia nos hortatur Scriptura, in quantum ista dilectio fraterna caritatem Dei includit ac præsupponit.
paras.en: But since without charity nothing is meritorious, it is added: [[4:8|But before all things|Ante omnia autem]], that is, chiefly and first of all, before all other exercises, [[4:8|have a constant mutual charity among yourselves|mutuam in vobismetipsis caritatem continuam habentes]], that is, unceasing brotherly charity, and, as far as is possible, actual charity too, so that we go forward constantly into the inward as well as the outward acts of charity, since the sign of charity is the carrying out of the act. Hence the Lord also says: [[John 15:12|This is my commandment, that you love one another, as I have loved you|Hoc est præceptum meum, ut diligatis invicem sicut dilexi vos]]. But since the first and greatest commandment is that God be loved with the whole heart, why is it that the prince of the Apostles exhorts us to love one another before all things? The answer is that the habitual charity [that is, charity as an abiding virtue in the soul, as distinct from its acts] by which we love God and our neighbour is one and the same, since God is the reason for loving our neighbours. And so the love of God and of neighbour embrace each other. Therefore, in our being admonished before all things to mutual charity, it is given to be understood that we should love God above all things and before all things; and so Scripture exhorts us to brotherly charity before all things, in so far as this brotherly love includes and presupposes the love of God.

paras.t: Quia caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum, id est, universa peccata ignis sanctæ dilectionis consumit et delet, non solum quantum ad culpam, sed etiam quantum ad pœnam, in toto aut in parte, secundum quod fervor amoris intensior fuerit sive remissior. Propter quod Christus dixit de beatissima Maria Magdalene: Dimissa sunt ei peccata multa, quoniam dilexit multum. In Proverbiis quoque Salomon ait: Universa delicta operit caritas. De hujus autem verbi expositione dicta sunt plura super illud Jacobi: Qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viæ suæ, salvabit animam ejus a morte, et operit multitudinem peccatorum.
paras.en: [[4:8|for charity covereth a multitude of sins|Quia caritas operit multitudinem peccatorum]]: that is, the fire of holy love consumes and blots out all sins, not only as to the guilt but also as to the punishment, wholly or in part, according as the fervour of love has been more intense or more slack. Therefore Christ said of the most blessed Mary Magdalene: [[Luke 7:47|Many sins are forgiven her, because she hath loved much|Dimissa sunt ei peccata multa, quoniam dilexit multum]]. In Proverbs too Solomon says: [[Prov 10:12|charity covereth all sins|Universa delicta operit caritas]]. On the explanation of this saying much was said on that verse of James: [[Jas 5:20|he who causeth a sinner to be converted from the error of his way shall save his soul from death and shall cover a multitude of sins|Qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viæ suæ, salvabit animam ejus a morte, et operit multitudinem peccatorum]].

paras.t: Hospitales invicem estote sine murmuratione, id est, patienter et gaudiose, gratis et caritative unus hospitet alium, et bene tractet eumdem. Præsertim autem religiosi peregrini et pauperes, sunt hospitandi et taliter repausandi. Istud namque est unum de operibus misericordiæ, quæ ad Christianos præcipue pertinent, et ad quæ caritas mutua specialiter obligat, ut scilicet unusquisque faciat alteri prout vult fieri sibi. Unde istud non observantibus Christus in die judicii est dicturus: Hospes fui, et non collegistis me. Hinc ad Hebræos dicitur: Caritas fraternitatis maneat vobiscum, et hospitalitatem nolite oblivisci; et Isaias, Egenos (inquit) vagosque induc in domum tuam. Quod sanctus Job implesse se pandit: Foris (inquiens) non mansit peregrinus; ostium meum viatori patuit.
paras.en: [[4:9|Using hospitality one towards another|Hospitales invicem estote]] [literally "Be hospitable to one another"] [[4:9|without murmuring|sine murmuratione]]: that is, patiently and joyfully, freely and charitably, let one give hospitality to another and treat him well. And especially religious, pilgrims and the poor are to be received as guests and so given rest. For this is one of the works of mercy, which belong especially to Christians and to which mutual charity especially binds us, namely that each should do to another as he would have done to himself[[Matt 7:12||]] [the margin gives Matth. xii, 12; the saying is at Matt 7:12]. Hence to those who do not keep this Christ will say on the day of judgment: [[Matt 25:43|I was a stranger and you took me not in|Hospes fui, et non collegistis me]]. Hence it is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:1|Let the charity of the brotherhood abide|Caritas fraternitatis maneat]] with you, [[Heb 13:2|and hospitality do not forget|et hospitalitatem nolite oblivisci]]; and Isaias says: [[Is 58:7|bring the needy and the harbourless into thy house|Egenos (inquit) vagosque induc in domum tuam]]. Which holy Job declares that he fulfilled, saying: [[Job 31:32|The stranger did not stay without|non mansit peregrinus]]; [[Job 31:32|my door was open to the traveller|ostium meum viatori patuit]].

paras.t: Nec solum hospitalitatem debet quilibet exercere, sed cetera quoque beneficia sibi a Deo collata, proximis communicare pro posse. Ideo sequitur: Unusquisque, sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes, id est, quilibet vestrum dona sibi desuper præstita, proximis suis pie et caritative diffundat, impendat, communicet: ut per ea fructificet Deo, impleatque quod Dominus ait, Negotiamini dum venio; et sic talenta sibi tradita virtuose multiplicet; et ita se habeat circa proximum quemadmodum Deus se habuit circa ipsum. Hoc totum est, ut opera misericordiæ, tam spiritualia quam corporalia, proximis impendat unusquisque pro posse. Cui ergo a Deo collata est major sapientia, aut major gratia exhortandi, aut major virtutum perfectio, libenter informet ac moneat alios, et eos conetur convertere. Propter quod ait Scriptura: Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus occultus, quæ utilitas in utrisque? Unde ad Colossenses dicitur: Docentes et commonentes vosmetipsos in hymnis et psalmis. In Apocalypsi quoque scriptum est: Qui audit, dicat, Veni. Hæc itaque agite, sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei, id est amorosi erogatores et communicatores multiplicium charismatum aut donorum Spiritus Sancti, quo uni datur sermo sapientiæ, alteri sermo scientiæ, alii gratia sanitatum, alii discretio spirituum, etc., prout ad Corinthios dicitur. Propter quod denuo loquitur Paulus: Unusquisque proprium donum habet a Deo. Ad hanc communicationem hortatur nos Salomon, dicens: Deriventur fontes tui foras. Et Christus: Luceat, inquit, lux vestra coram hominibus. Est itaque Dei gratia multiformis, id est varia ac diversa, multipliciterque distincta.
paras.en: And not only ought everyone to practise hospitality, but also to share with his neighbours, as far as he can, the other benefits bestowed on him by God. Therefore there follows: [[4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque, sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]]: that is, let each of you pour out, spend and share with his neighbours, devoutly and charitably, the gifts bestowed on him from above, so that through them he may bear fruit to God and fulfil what the Lord says: [[Luke 19:13|Trade till I come|Negotiamini dum venio]]; and so may virtuously multiply the talents entrusted to him, and behave towards his neighbour as God has behaved towards him. The whole of it is this: that each should bestow on his neighbours, as far as he can, the works of mercy, spiritual as well as bodily. Let him, then, on whom God has bestowed greater wisdom, or a greater grace of exhorting, or a greater perfection of virtues, gladly instruct and admonish others and try to convert them. Therefore Scripture says: [[Ecclus 20:32|Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is not seen: what profit is there in them both?|Sapientia abscondita et thesaurus occultus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?]] [the same words stand at Ecclus 41:17]. Hence it is said to the Colossians: [[Col 3:16|teaching and admonishing one another|Docentes et commonentes vosmetipsos]] in hymns and psalms. In the Apocalypse too it is written: [[Apoc 22:17|he that heareth, let him say: Come|Qui audit, dicat, Veni]]. Do these things, then, [[4:10|as good stewards of the manifold grace of God|sicut boni dispensatores multiformis gratiæ Dei]]: that is, as loving dispensers and sharers of the manifold charisms or gifts of the Holy Ghost, by whom to one [[1 Cor 12:8|is given the word of wisdom|datur sermo sapientiæ]], to another [[1 Cor 12:8|the word of knowledge|sermo scientiæ]], to another [[1 Cor 12:9|the grace of healing|gratia sanitatum]], to another [[1 Cor 12:10|the discerning of spirits|discretio spirituum]], etc., as is said to the Corinthians. Therefore Paul says again: [[1 Cor 7:7|every one hath his proper gift from God|Unusquisque proprium donum habet a Deo]]. To this sharing Solomon exhorts us, saying: [[Prov 5:16|Let thy fountains be conveyed abroad|Deriventur fontes tui foras]]. And Christ: [[Matt 5:16|let your light|Luceat]], He says, [[Matt 5:16|shine before men|lux vestra coram hominibus]]. The grace of God, then, is manifold, that is, various and diverse, and distinguished in many ways.

paras.t: Et potest per gratiam Dei hoc loco intelligi omne donum gratis a Deo impensum, per quod unus potest alteri aliquo modo prodesse. Specialiter tamen potest hic locus exponi de donis gratiæ gratis datæ, quæ ad aliorum dantur utilitatem. Specialiter quoque administratio seu communicatio ista ad prælatos, prædicatores, doctoresque pertinent, ut cum Psalmista dicere valeant Deo: Justitiam tuam non abscondi in corde meo, veritatem tuam et salutare tuum dixi; et illud Sapientiæ: Non abscondam a vobis sacramenta Dei, neque cum invidia tabescente iter habebo, sed dona Dei communico vobis.
paras.en: And by the grace of God can be understood in this place every gift freely bestowed by God, through which one can in some way profit another. Specially, however, this place can be explained of the gifts of grace freely given [*gratia gratis data*: gifts such as prophecy or the word of wisdom, given for the good of others rather than for the holiness of the one who has them], which are given for the profit of others. Specially too this ministering or sharing belongs to prelates, preachers and doctors, so that with the Psalmist they may be able to say to God: [[Ps 39:11|I have not hid thy justice within my heart: I have declared thy truth and thy salvation|Justitiam tuam non abscondi in corde meo, veritatem tuam et salutare tuum dixi]]; and that saying of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:24|I will not hide from you the mysteries of God|Non abscondam a vobis sacramenta Dei]], [[Wis 6:25|Neither will I go with consuming envy|neque cum invidia tabescente iter habebo]], but I share the gifts of God with you[[Wis 7:13||]] [the margin gives Sap. v, 24, 25; the words are at Wis 6:24–25, and the last clause recalls Wis 7:13, "communicate without envy"].

paras.t: Si quis loquitur, quasi sermones Dei, id est, non nisi de Deo loquatur, ita ut ad minus verba sua ad Dei referat gloriam et honorem, sintque utilia, juxta illud ad Ephesios: Omnis sermo malus ex ore vestro non procedat, sed qui utilis est ad ædificationem, ut det gratiam audienti. Vel, Quasi sermones Dei, id est, non aliud quis loquatur aut doceat, quam quod consonum est Scripturis vel continetur in eis. Propter quod Timotheo scripsit apostolus Paulus: Profanas vocum novitates devita. Vel, Quasi sermones Dei, id est, Deo adscribat quidquid boni aut salubriter dixerit. Non enim sufficientes sumus cogitare aliquid ex nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est. Hinc scriptum est: In manu Dei sumus, et nos, et sermones nostri.
paras.en: [[4:11|If any man speak|Si quis loquitur]], let him speak, [[4:11|as the words of God|quasi sermones Dei]]: that is, let him speak only of God, so that at least he refers his words to the glory and honour of God, and they are profitable, according to that saying to the Ephesians: [[Eph 4:29|Let no evil speech proceed from your mouth|Omnis sermo malus ex ore vestro non procedat]], but that which is profitable [[Eph 4:29|to the edification|ad ædificationem]], [[Eph 4:29|that it may administer grace|ut det gratiam]] to the hearer. Or, [[4:11|as the words of God|Quasi sermones Dei]]: that is, let no one say or teach anything other than what agrees with the Scriptures or is contained in them. Therefore the Apostle Paul wrote to Timothy: Avoid [[1 Tim 6:20|the profane novelties of words|Profanas vocum novitates]]. Or, [[4:11|as the words of God|Quasi sermones Dei]]: that is, let him ascribe to God whatever good or wholesome thing he has said. For we are not [[2 Cor 3:5|sufficient to think any thing of ourselves, as of ourselves: but our sufficiency is from God|sufficientes sumus cogitare aliquid ex nobis, quasi ex nobis, sed sufficientia nostra ex Deo est]]. Hence it is written: [[Wis 7:16|in his hand are both we, and our words|In manu Dei sumus, et nos, et sermones nostri]] [the margin gives Sap. xvi, 26; the words are at Wis 7:16].

paras.t: Si quis ministrat, id est, bonum quodcumque alteri exhibet seu impendit, tanquam ex virtute quam administrat Deus, id est, non propria virtute, sed virtute sibi a Deo collata id se facere arbitretur, et omne bonum quod habet aut aliis impartitur, Deo tanquam superdignissimo fonti liberalissimoque datori, grata ac humili mente attribuat, quum dicat Salvator: Sine me nihil potestis facere; et Paulus, Quid habes quod non accepisti?
paras.en: [[4:11|If any minister|Si quis ministrat]], that is, shows or bestows any good thing on another, let him do it [[4:11|as of the power which God administereth|tanquam ex virtute quam administrat Deus]]: that is, let him reckon that he does it not by his own power but by the power bestowed on him by God, and let him attribute every good that he has or imparts to others to God, as to the supremely worthy fountain and most liberal giver, with a grateful and humble mind, since the Saviour says: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and Paul: [[1 Cor 4:7|what hast thou that thou hast not received|Quid habes quod non accepisti?]]?

paras.t: Ut in omnibus honorificetur, id est, debito modo a vobis ac aliis honoretur, Deus Trinitas per Jesum Christum Dei et hominum mediatorem, hominem verum, Dominum nostrum, cujus virtute et merito gratiarum charismata nobis desuper infunduntur. Hoc est quod ait Salvator : Videant opera vestra bona, et glorificent Patrem vestrum, qui in cœlis est. Vas quoque electionis Corinthiis scribens : Omnia, inquit, in gloriam Dei facite; et ad Colossenses, Omne quodcumque facitis in verbo aut in opere, omnia in nomine Domini agite, gratias agentes Deo.
paras.en: [[4:11|that in all things God may be honoured|Ut in omnibus honorificetur]], that is, that God the Trinity may be honoured in due manner by you and by others, [[4:11|through Jesus Christ|per Jesum Christum]], the [[1 Tim 2:5|mediator of God and men|Dei et hominum mediatorem]], true man, our Lord, by whose power and merit the gifts of graces are poured into us from above. This is what the Saviour says: [[Matt 5:16|that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven|Videant opera vestra bona, et glorificent Patrem vestrum, qui in cœlis est]]. The Vessel of election too, writing to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 10:31|do all|Omnia]], he says, [[1 Cor 10:31|to the glory of God|in gloriam Dei facite]]; and to the Colossians: [[Col 3:17|All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God|Omne quodcumque facitis in verbo aut in opere, omnia in nomine Domini agite, gratias agentes Deo]].

paras.t: Cui est gloria et imperium in sæcula sæculorum. Amen. De quo ait apostolus Paulus : Regi sæculorum immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria. Ipse est enim rex omnipotens, in cujus ditione cuncta sunt posita. Est autem Deo gloria, id est infinita lætitia, clara quoque cum laude notitia, et immensa majestas.
paras.en: [[4:11|to whom is glory and empire for ever and ever. Amen|Cui est gloria et imperium in sæcula sæculorum. Amen]]. Of whom the apostle Paul says: [[1 Tim 1:17|to the king of ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory|Regi sæculorum immortali, invisibili, soli Deo honor et gloria]]. For he is the [[Esth 13:9|almighty king|rex omnipotens]], in whose dominion all things are placed [Denis is using the words of Mardochai's prayer, Esth 13:9; the margin note beside them cannot be read]. Now the glory of God is infinite joy, a clear knowledge joined with praise, and boundless majesty.

paras.t: Præterea, denuo redit Archiapostolus ad exhortandum fideles, ut habeant insuperabilem patientiam in adversis. Carissimi, nolite peregrinari, id est a fide fieri alieni, aut a Deo alienatos et exteros vos putare, in fervore, id est persecutionum impetu vehementi seu furioso, qui ad tentationem vobis fit, id est, vobis ab incredulis ac perversis, Deo permittente, infligitur ad vestri probationem et coronationem : quamvis impii alia intentione vos persequantur. Sed Deo disponente, omnia cooperantur electis in bonum. De hoc dicta sunt multa super illud Jacobi : Beatus vir qui suffert tentationem, quoniam quum probatus fuerit, etc. Itaque ex hac re, Nolite peregrinari; vel (ut alia littera, qua utitur Beda, habet), Nolite mirari; quasi novi aliquid vobis contingat. Istud enim novum non est, sed ut dixit Judith : Omnes qui Deo placuerunt, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles; et Sapiens, Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit electos Dominus. Psalmista quoque : Multæ, inquit, tribulationes justorum. Hoc est quod in Proverbiis scribitur : Sicut igne probatur argentum, et aurum camino, ita corda probat Dominus. Hinc ait venerabilis Beda : In Ecclesia a protomartyre Abel, usque ad ultimum qui in fine mundi nascetur electum, nunquam persecutio desinet. Imo, ut electionis Vas protestatur, per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum Dei.
paras.en: Further, the Archapostle returns once more to exhorting the faithful to have unconquerable patience in adversity. [[4:12|Dearly beloved, think not strange|Carissimi, nolite peregrinari]] [the Latin *nolite peregrinari* is literally *do not be strangers* or *do not go abroad*; Denis's expositions turn on this], that is, do not become strangers to the faith, nor think yourselves estranged from God and foreigners to him, [[4:12|the burning heat|in fervore]], that is, the vehement or furious onset of persecutions, [[4:12|which is to try you|qui ad tentationem vobis fit]], that is, which, God permitting, is inflicted on you by unbelievers and perverse men for your proving and crowning, although the wicked persecute you with another intention. But, God so disposing, [[Rom 8:28|all things work together|omnia cooperantur]] for the elect [[Rom 8:28|unto good|in bonum]]. Much has been said of this on that saying of James: [[Jas 1:12|Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for, when he hath been proved|Beatus vir qui suffert tentationem, quoniam quum probatus fuerit]], etc. Therefore, on this account, [[4:12|think not strange|Nolite peregrinari]]; or (as another reading, which Bede uses, has it), Do not wonder; [[4:12|as if some new thing happened to you|quasi novi aliquid vobis contingat]]. For this is not new; but, as Judith said: [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Omnes qui Deo placuerunt, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]; and the Wise man: [[Wis 3:6|As gold in the furnace|Tanquam aurum in fornace]] the Lord [[Wis 3:6|hath proved|probavit]] his elect. The Psalmist also: [[Ps 33:20|Many|Multæ]], he says, [[Ps 33:20|are the afflictions of the just|tribulationes justorum]]. This is what is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 17:3|As silver is tried by fire, and gold in the furnace: so the Lord trieth the hearts|Sicut igne probatur argentum, et aurum camino, ita corda probat Dominus]]. Hence the venerable Bede says: In the Church, from the protomartyr Abel to the last elect one who shall be born at the end of the world, persecution will never cease. Indeed, as the Vessel of election declares, [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum Dei]].

paras.t: Sed quum in secunda ad Corinthios dicatur, Dum sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino : quid est quod princeps nunc ait Apostolorum : Nolite peregrinari in fervore, etc., quum fervor iste non nisi in corpore isto mortali eveniat?
paras.en: But since it is said in the second Epistle to the Corinthians, [[2 Cor 5:6|while we are in the body we are absent from the Lord|Dum sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino]] [the Latin has the same verb, *peregrinamur*, we are abroad, on pilgrimage], what is it that the prince of the Apostles now says, [[4:12|think not strange the burning heat|Nolite peregrinari in fervore]], etc., when this burning heat befalls only in this mortal body?

paras.t: Ad hoc respondetur ex verbis Alberti, quod aliquis dicitur peregrinari quatuor modis : Primo, propter distantiam loci. Et isto modo in hoc sæculo dicimur peregrinari, quoniam multum distamus a cœlo empyreo, quod est locus et patria electorum. Hinc ait Propheta : Heu mihi ! quia incolatus meus prolongatus est. Secundo, propter corporis hujus corruptibilitatem, et statum mortalem ac corpulentum. Sicque loquitur Paulus : Dum sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino. Verius tamen intelligitur peregrinatio ista propter spiritualem distantiam cognitionis hujus imperfectæ a perfecta notitia Dei, quam habent Beati. Propter quod præallegatis verbis protinus addit Apostolus : Per fidem enim ambulamus, non per speciem. Tertio, propter temporis elongationem. Propter quod in Genesi ait Jacob patriarcha : Dies peregrinationis meæ super terram, centum triginta anni sunt. Quarto, propter carentiam gratiæ ac providentiæ Dei. Et sic nullus fidelis debet se reputare peregrinum a Deo propter tribulationes quas patitur, quasi ob hoc sit a Deo relictus, et quasi Deus providentiam actuum non habeat humanorum, quoniam justos ab impiis tribulari permittit : imo hoc ipsum est præcipuum signum suæ providentiæ ac prædestinationis circa electos, quum per Zachariam protestetur : Ducam eos per ignem, et uram eos sicut uritur argentum, et probabo eos sicut probatur aurum.
paras.en: To this the answer is given from the words of Albert, that one is said to be a pilgrim [*peregrinari*, to be abroad, away from home] in four ways. First, by distance of place. And in this way we are said to be pilgrims in this world, since we are far distant from the empyrean heaven, which is the place and fatherland of the elect. Hence the Prophet says: [[Ps 119:5|Woe is me, that my sojourning is prolonged|Heu mihi ! quia incolatus meus prolongatus est]]. Secondly, by the corruptibility of this body, and its mortal and bodily state. And so Paul says: [[2 Cor 5:6|while we are in the body we are absent from the Lord|Dum sumus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino]]. Yet this pilgrimage is more truly understood of the spiritual distance of this imperfect knowledge from the perfect knowledge of God which the Blessed have. For which reason, straight after the words quoted, the Apostle adds: [[2 Cor 5:7|For we walk by faith and not by sight|Per fidem enim ambulamus, non per speciem]]. Thirdly, by length of time. For which reason the patriarch Jacob says in Genesis: [[Gen 47:9|The days of my pilgrimage|Dies peregrinationis meæ]] upon earth [[Gen 47:9|are a hundred and thirty years|centum triginta anni sunt]]. Fourthly, by lack of the grace and providence of God. And in this sense no believer ought to reckon himself a stranger to God because of the tribulations he suffers, as though on that account he were forsaken by God, and as though God had no providence over human acts because he permits the just to be afflicted by the wicked; nay, this very thing is the chief sign of his providence and predestination towards the elect, since he declares through Zacharias: [[Zach 13:9|I will bring|Ducam eos]] them [[Zach 13:9|through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined: and I will try them as gold is tried|per ignem, et uram eos sicut uritur argentum, et probabo eos sicut probatur aurum]].

paras.t: Quidam hunc locum ita exponunt : Nolite peregrinari, id est ad alia loca vos transferre, in fervore, etc., id est ex timore persecutionum. Nam, quamvis interdum liceat fugere, Christo dicente, Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam; tamen perfectius est manere, nisi sit persecutio certæ personæ, cujus fuga utilior est Ecclesiæ quam ejus festinatum martyrium, et propter majus bonum Ecclesiæ, non ex mortis timore, ineat fugam, sicut Paulus de Damasco clam fugit.
paras.en: Some expound this place thus: [[4:12|think not strange|Nolite peregrinari]] [here taken as *do not go abroad*], that is, do not remove yourselves to other places, [[4:12|the burning heat|in fervore]], etc., that is, for fear of persecutions. For although it is sometimes lawful to flee, as Christ says, [[Matt 10:23|when they shall persecute you in this city, flee into another|Quum persecuti vos fuerint in una civitate, fugite in aliam]] [the margin gives Matth. v, 23; the words are at Matt 10:23], yet it is more perfect to remain; unless it is the persecution of a particular person whose flight is more useful to the Church than his hastened martyrdom, and he takes to flight for the greater good of the Church, not from fear of death, as Paul fled secretly from Damascus[[2 Cor 11:33||]].

paras.t: Sequitur : Sed communicantes Christi passionibus, gaudete, id est, imitatione, intuitu et amore Christi propter vos passi, patiendo adversa gaudete in Domino : propter multiplicem fructum vobis inde provenientem ; imo potissime, quia hoc complacet Deo in vobis, et quia hoc dignum et justum est, ut suo capiti membra assimilentur. Propter quod ait ipse : Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlo; et Jacobus, Omne (inquit) gaudium existimate, quum in diversas tentationes incideritis.
paras.en: There follows: [[4:13|But if you partake of the sufferings of Christ, rejoice|Sed communicantes Christi passionibus, gaudete]], that is, in imitation, contemplation and love of Christ who suffered for you, rejoice in the Lord while you suffer adversity, for the manifold fruit that comes to you from it; nay, chiefly because this is pleasing to God in you, and because it is fitting and just that the members be made like their head. For which reason he himself says: [[Matt 5:12|Be glad and rejoice for your reward is very great in heaven|Gaudete in illa hora et exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa est in cœlo]] [Denis's *in illa hora*, in that hour, recalls Luke 6:23]; and James: [[Jas 1:2|count it all joy, when you shall fall into divers temptations|Omne (inquit) gaudium existimate, quum in diversas tentationes incideritis]].

paras.t: Ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus, id est in aperta visione excellentiæ Christi, gaudeatis exsultantes, id est, tam vehementer gaudentes interius, ut redundet illud gaudium internum in corpus post resurrectionem futuram. Propter quod ait Psalmista : Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua.
paras.en: [[4:13|that, when his glory shall be revealed|Ut et in revelatione gloriæ ejus]], that is, in the open vision of the excellence of Christ, [[4:13|you may also be glad with exceeding joy|gaudeatis exsultantes]], that is, rejoicing so vehemently within that this inward joy will overflow into the body after the resurrection to come. For which reason the Psalmist says: [[Ps 16:15|I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear|Satiabor quum apparuerit gloria tua]].

paras.t: Præterea Christi passionibus, quas pro nobis sustinuit, debemus variis modis communicare : Primo, eas in nostro corpore per imitationem assidue deferendo, corpus proprium in operibus pœnitentiæ affligendo, seu aliis tribulationibus propter Deum viriliter exponendo. Unde secunda ad Corinthios fassus est Paulus : In omnibus tribulationem patimur, sed non angustiamur; semper mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes, ut et vita Jesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali. Et ad Philippenses : In omni, ait, fiducia magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem. Secundo, de eis gaudendo propter summos et multiplices fructus earum : quia per eas placatus est Deus, et liberatum est genus humanum a morte æterna, purgatum quoque a morte peccati, et particeps factus est homo gratiæ in præsenti, et gloriæ in futuro; spiritusque maligni sunt victi. Idcirco ad Galatas locutus est Paulus : Mihi absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini mei Jesu Christi. Tertio, de imitatione cruciformi earum lætando, sicut Apostoli ibant gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati, ut scribitur in Actibus. Quarto, de merito passionis Christi et imitatione ejusdem, beatitudinem exspectando, quemadmodum secunda ad Corinthios inducitur : Scitote quoniam sicut socii passionum estis, sic eritis et consolationis. Secunda quoque ad Timotheum : Si commortui sumus, et convivemus ; si sustinemus, et conregnabimus. Quinto, dominicam passionem quotidie cum pia et intima compassione reminiscendo, secundum illud ad Hebræos : Recogitate eum qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversum semetipsum contradictionem. Et in Threnis scriptum est : Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea. Sexto, pro Christo martyrium sustinendo : qui tamen modus comprehendi potest sub primo. — Quum ergo non sit servus major domino suo, non renuamus exemplo Christi, et ejus intuitu ac amore, tribulationibus exerceri, adversa pati, castigari, ac corripi. Imo gaudeamus in talibus, sicut in omnibus divitiis, ut cum Paulo dicere valeamus : Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto ; et item, Christo confixus sum cruci.
paras.en: Moreover, we ought in various ways to [[4:13|partake of the sufferings of Christ|Christi passionibus]], which he bore for us. First, by bearing them constantly in our body through imitation, afflicting our own body in works of penance, or manfully exposing it to other tribulations for God's sake. Hence Paul confessed in the second Epistle to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 4:8|In all things we suffer tribulation: but are not distressed|In omnibus tribulationem patimur, sed non angustiamur]]; [[2 Cor 4:10|Always bearing about in our body the mortification of Jesus|semper mortificationem Jesu in corpore nostro circumferentes]], [[2 Cor 4:11|that the life also of Jesus may be made manifest in our mortal flesh|ut et vita Jesu manifestetur in carne nostra mortali]]. And to the Philippians he says: [[Phil 1:20|with all confidence|In omni, ait, fiducia]] [[Phil 1:20|shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether it be by life or by death|magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem]]. Secondly, by rejoicing in them for their supreme and manifold fruits: for through them God was appeased, mankind was set free from eternal death and cleansed also from the death of sin, man was made partaker of grace in the present and of glory in the future, and the wicked spirits were vanquished. Therefore Paul said to the Galatians: [[Gal 6:14|God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ|Mihi absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini mei Jesu Christi]]. Thirdly, by being glad of the imitation of them in the form of the cross, as the Apostles [[Acts 5:41|went from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus|ibant gaudentes a conspectu concilii, quoniam digni habiti sunt pro nomine Jesu contumeliam pati]], as is written in the Acts. Fourthly, by awaiting beatitude from the merit of Christ's passion and from the imitation of it, as is set down in the second Epistle to the Corinthians: [[2 Cor 1:7|knowing that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation|Scitote quoniam sicut socii passionum estis, sic eritis et consolationis]]. In the second to Timothy also: [[2 Tim 2:11|if we be dead with him, we shall live also with him|Si commortui sumus, et convivemus]]; [[2 Tim 2:12|If we suffer, we shall also reign with him|si sustinemus, et conregnabimus]]. Fifthly, by recalling the Lord's passion daily with loving and heartfelt compassion, according to that word to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:3|think diligently upon him that endured such opposition from sinners against himself|Recogitate eum qui talem sustinuit a peccatoribus adversum semetipsum contradictionem]]. And in Lamentations it is written: [[Lam 3:20|I will be mindful and remember, and my soul shall languish within me|Memoria memor ero, et tabescet in me anima mea]]. Sixthly, by suffering martyrdom for Christ; though this way can be included under the first. Since, then, the [[John 15:20|servant is not greater than his master|non sit servus major domino suo]] [the margin gives Joann. xv, 16; the words are at John 15:20, and also John 13:16], let us not refuse, after the example of Christ and in contemplation and love of him, to be exercised by tribulations, to suffer adversity, to be chastised and rebuked. Nay, let us rejoice in such things as in all riches, so that we may be able to say with Paul: [[Gal 6:17|I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body|Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto]]; and again: [[Gal 2:19|with Christ I am nailed to the cross|Christo confixus sum cruci]].

paras.t: Sed et si exprobramini, id est, per verba contumeliosa et injuriosa vituperamini a perfidis et iniquis hominibus, in nomine Christi, id est idcirco quia in Christum creditis, aut secundum ejus doctrinam præceptaque vivitis, beati eritis, nunc in spe et merito, deinde in re et præmio, dummodo æquanimiter ex caritate sustineatis, et usque in finem in bonis perseveretis. Hoc est quod Christus affirmat : Beati eritis quum vos oderint homines, et quum separaverint vos, et exprobraverint, et ejecerint nomen vestrum tanquam malum, propter Filium hominis. Gaudete in illa hora : ecce enim merces vestra multa est in cœlo. Hinc loquitur Augustinus : Socii contumeliæ, erunt et socii gloriæ. Idcirco nunc subditur :
paras.en: But also, [[4:14|If you be reproached|si exprobramini]], that is, if you are reviled with insulting and injurious words by faithless and wicked men, [[4:14|for the name of Christ|in nomine Christi]], that is, because you believe in Christ, or live according to his teaching and precepts, [[4:14|you shall be blessed|beati eritis]], now in hope and merit, afterwards in reality and reward, provided that you bear it with equanimity out of charity, and persevere in good to the end.
