This is what Christ affirms: [[Luke 6:22|Blessed shall you be when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you and shall reproach you and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake|Beati eritis quum vos oderint homines, et quum separaverint vos, et exprobraverint, et ejecerint nomen vestrum tanquam malum, propter Filium hominis]]. [[Luke 6:23|Be glad|Gaudete]] in that hour [Luke has *in that day*]: [[Luke 6:23|for behold, your reward is great in heaven|ecce enim merces vestra multa est in cœlo]]. Hence Augustine says: Companions in reproach, they will also be companions in glory. Therefore there is now added:

paras.t: Quoniam quod est honoris, gloriæ et virtutis Dei, id est honor quem Deus retribuit justis pro eorum actibus virtuosis (nam honor debetur virtuti), et gloria seu beatitudo quæ eorum meritis correspondet, in quantum ex caritate procedunt, et virtus seu constantia aut fortitudo qua Deus suos in adversis confortat, et qui est ejus Spiritus, id est Spiritus Sanctus, qui est Spiritus Christi, sicut et Patris, quoniam a Patre et Filio tanquam ex uno fonte atque eodem principio est procedens, quemadmodum Filius ait de Spiritu Sancto : Ille me clarificabit, quia de meo accipiet. Paulus quoque fatetur : Si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est ejus. Super vos requiescit, id est, in cordibus vestris est unumquodque istorum.
paras.en: [[4:14|for that which is of the honour, glory and power of God|Quoniam quod est honoris, gloriæ et virtutis Dei]], that is, the honour which God renders to the just for their virtuous acts (for honour is owed to virtue), and the glory or beatitude which answers to their merits, inasmuch as these proceed from charity, and the power [the Latin *virtus* is both power and virtue], or constancy or fortitude, by which God strengthens his own in adversity, [[4:14|and that which is his Spirit|et qui est ejus Spiritus]], that is, the Holy Ghost, who is the Spirit of Christ as of the Father, since he proceeds from the Father and the Son as from one fountain and one and the same principle, as the Son says of the Holy Ghost: [[John 16:14|He shall glorify me: because he shall receive of mine|Ille me clarificabit, quia de meo accipiet]]. Paul also declares: [[Rom 8:9|if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his|Si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est ejus]]. [[4:14|resteth upon you|Super vos requiescit]], that is, each of these is in your hearts.

paras.t: Nam honor et gloria quæ in patria præstantur electis fidelibus, sunt modo in eis per inchoationem et spem ac meritum, et radicaliter atque causaliter. Est item in eis formaliter virtus a Deo infusa, et Dei confortatio gratiosa. Sed et Spiritus Sanctus in omni virtuoso, humili et quieto quiescere perhibetur, prout apud Isaiam loquitur Deus : Super quem requiescet Spiritus meus, nisi super quietum et humilem? — Potest et ita intelligi : Quod est honoris, gloriæ et virtutis, id est, quod Deus reputat honorabile, gloriosum et virtuosum, seu triumphale, videlicet invicta patientia in adversis, requiescit in vobis. Requiescit etiam Spiritus Sanctus super electos et justos, tanquam pius sessor et ductor eorum, dirigens eos quomodo vult, juxta illud : Justum deduxit Dominus per vias rectas. Propter quod loquitur Paulus : Quicumque Spiritu Dei aguntur, hi filii sunt Dei.
paras.en: For the honour and glory which are bestowed on the faithful elect in the fatherland are in them now by way of beginning, of hope and of merit, in their root and in their cause. Likewise there is in them formally the virtue infused by God, and God's gracious strengthening. And the Holy Ghost, too, is said to rest in everyone who is virtuous, humble and quiet, as God says in Isaias: Upon whom shall my Spirit rest, but upon him that is quiet and humble?[[Is 66:2||]] [the margin gives Cf. Is. lxvi, 1, 2; Denis quotes the old Latin reading of Is 66:2, where the Vulgate has: to whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little, and of a contrite spirit]. It can also be understood thus: [[4:14|that which is of the honour, glory and power|Quod est honoris, gloriæ et virtutis]], that is, what God reckons honourable, glorious and virtuous, or triumphant, namely unconquered patience in adversity, [[4:14|resteth upon you|requiescit in vobis]]. The Holy Ghost also rests upon the elect and the just as their loving rider and guide, directing them as he wills, according to that word: The Lord [[Wis 10:10|conducted the just|Justum deduxit]] [[Wis 10:10|through the right ways|per vias rectas]]. For which reason Paul says: [[Rom 8:14|whosoever are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God|Quicumque Spiritu Dei aguntur, hi filii sunt Dei]].

paras.t: Nemo autem vestrum patiatur ut homicida, aut fur, aut maledicus, id est convitiosa verba in alium proferens, seu maledicens, aut alienorum appetitor, id est res aliorum auferre desiderans : hoc est, nolite hæc aut consimilia vitia perpetrare, nec per ea temporalem afflictionem et mortem mereri : præsertim quia in primitiva Ecclesia hoc fuisset valde derogativum justorum fidelium, et causa desertionis fidei christianæ a pertolis, blasphemationisque Christi. Si tamen (quod absit) quis vitia ista commiserit, debet debitam punitionem pro eis patienter sufferre, ut in futuro misericordiam consequatur.
paras.en: [[4:15|But let none of you suffer as a murderer or a thief or a railer|Nemo autem vestrum patiatur ut homicida, aut fur, aut maledicus]], that is, one who utters abusive words against another, or curses, [[4:15|or coveter of other men's things|aut alienorum appetitor]], that is, one who desires to take away the goods of others: that is, do not commit these or like vices, nor deserve temporal affliction and death through them; above all because in the primitive Church this would have greatly discredited the just among the faithful, and been a cause of desertion of the Christian faith by the weak [the print has *a pertolis*, apparently a misprint; the sense seems to be *by the weak* or *the little ones*], and of blasphemy against Christ. If, however, anyone (which God forbid) has committed these vices, he ought to bear the due punishment for them patiently, so that he may obtain mercy in the time to come.

paras.t: Si autem ut Christianus, id est, si patitur quia in Christum credit et ei obedit, non erubescat, quum non sit inhonestum seu erubescibile, sed justum et honore dignissimum, taliter pati. Ideo subditur : glorificet autem Deum in isto nomine, id est, Deum collaudet, et ei regratietur quod ei concessit hanc gratiam, ut scilicet pro justitia patiatur, et Christo sic conformetur. Nam et in Christum credere, et bona agere, ac pro justitia pati, dona sunt Dei, prout ad Philippenses asseritur : Vobis donatum est pro Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, sed etiam ut pro illo patiamini.
paras.en: [[4:16|But, if as a Christian|Si autem ut Christianus]], that is, if he suffers because he believes in Christ and obeys him, [[4:16|let him not be ashamed|non erubescat]], since it is not dishonourable or shameful, but just and most worthy of honour, to suffer so. Therefore it is added: [[4:16|but let him glorify God in that name|glorificet autem Deum in isto nomine]], that is, let him praise God and thank him for granting him this grace, namely to suffer for justice and so be conformed to Christ. For to believe in Christ, to do good and to suffer for justice are gifts of God, as is declared to the Philippians: [[Phil 1:29|unto you it is given for Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer for him|Vobis donatum est pro Christo, non solum ut credatis in eum, sed etiam ut pro illo patiamini]].

paras.t: Quoniam tempus est ut incipiat judicium a domo Dei, id est, in sæculo isto electi et justi, qui sunt vera et viva membra domus Dei, puta Ecclesiæ militantis, variis modis exercentur adversis, secundum ordinationem occulti judicii Dei, qui interdum per angelos sanctos castigat electos, interdum permittit eos a pravis hominibus atque dæmonibus flagellari sive occidi. In primitiva quoque Ecclesia tempus fuit persecutionis gravissimæ Christianorum, qui ab impiis morti adjudicabantur quotidie et trucidabantur. Propter quod ait Salvator : Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo; et alibi, Ego (inquit) quos amo, arguo et castigo. Per Ezechielem etiam loquitur Dominus : A sanctuario meo incipite percutere.
paras.en: [[4:17|For the time is, that judgment should begin at the house of God|Quoniam tempus est ut incipiat judicium a domo Dei]], that is, in this world the elect and the just, who are the true and living members of the house of God, namely of the Church militant, are exercised by adversities in various ways according to the ordering of the hidden judgment of God, who sometimes chastises the elect through the holy angels, and sometimes permits them to be scourged or slain by wicked men and by demons. In the primitive Church also there was a time of most grievous persecution of the Christians, who were daily condemned to death by the wicked and slaughtered. For which reason the Saviour says: [[John 16:2|the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth a service to God|Venit hora, ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo]]; and elsewhere he says: [[Apoc 3:19|Such as I love|Ego (inquit) quos amo]], [[Apoc 3:19|I rebuke and chastise|arguo et castigo]]. Through Ezechiel too the Lord says: [[Ezech 9:6|begin ye at my sanctuary|A sanctuario meo incipite]] to strike.

paras.t: Si autem primum a nobis, id est, si justi, fideles, electi in primis ita quotidie patiuntur adversa, et dijudicantur ab impiis; quis finis eorum qui non credunt Dei Evangelio? id est, qualis et quanta erit incredulorum et reproborum damnatio, super quos non est virga Dei in vita præsenti, sed eorum vita est impunita nequitia, et lætantur quum malefecerint? quasi dicat : Valde dura erit illorum punitio in futuro, et quanto nunc diutius tolerantur, tanto tunc gravius damnabuntur. Unde in Joanne legitur : Qui non credit, jam judicatus est, quia non credit in nomine unigeniti Filii Dei. Hinc secunda ad Thessalonicenses habetur : Gloriamur pro patientia vestra in omnibus persecutionibus quas sustinetis in exemplum justi judicii Dei : si tamen justum est apud Deum, retribuere tribulationem his qui vos tribulant, in revelatione Domini Jesu Christi de cœlo, cum angelis, in flamma ignis dantis vindictam his qui non obediunt Evangelio, qui pœnas dabunt in interitu æternas a facie Domini, et a gloria virtutis ejus, quum venerit glorificari in Sanctis suis.
paras.en: [[4:17|And if at first at us|Si autem primum a nobis]], that is, if the just, the faithful, the elect, first of all, suffer adversity thus daily and are condemned by the wicked, [[4:17|what shall be the end of them that believe not the gospel of God?|quis finis eorum qui non credunt Dei Evangelio?]] that is, of what kind and how great will be the damnation of the unbelieving and the reprobate, over whom there is no rod of God in the present life, but whose life is unpunished wickedness, and who rejoice when they have done evil? As if to say: very hard will be their punishment hereafter, and the longer they are borne with now, the more heavily will they then be condemned. Hence we read in John: [[John 3:18|he that doth not believe is already judged: because he believeth not in the name of the only begotten Son of God|Qui non credit, jam judicatus est, quia non credit in nomine unigeniti Filii Dei]]. Hence it is said in the second Epistle to the Thessalonians: We [[2 Thess 1:4|glory|Gloriamur]] [[2 Thess 1:4|for your patience|pro patientia vestra]] [[2 Thess 1:4|in all your persecutions and tribulations: which you endure|in omnibus persecutionibus quas sustinetis]] for [[2 Thess 1:5|an example of the just judgment of God|in exemplum justi judicii Dei]]: [[2 Thess 1:6|Seeing it is a just thing with God to repay tribulation to them that trouble you|si tamen justum est apud Deum, retribuere tribulationem his qui vos tribulant]], [[2 Thess 1:7|when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with the angels|in revelatione Domini Jesu Christi de cœlo, cum angelis]], [[2 Thess 1:8|In a flame of fire, giving vengeance to them|in flamma ignis dantis vindictam his]] [[2 Thess 1:8|who obey not the gospel|qui non obediunt Evangelio]]; [[2 Thess 1:9|Who shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction, from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power|qui pœnas dabunt in interitu æternas a facie Domini, et a gloria virtutis ejus]], [[2 Thess 1:10|When he shall come to be glorified in his saints|quum venerit glorificari in Sanctis suis]].

paras.t: Denique ex his sumitur evidens argumentum veritatis fidei christianæ. Videmus enim homines pessimos sanitate et prosperitate usque ad senectutem potiri, homines vero timoratos, justos ac devotissimos, omni tempore tribulationibus et adversitatibus exerceri. Si ergo non est vita post præsentem alia, in qua fiat retributio justa, ubi est justitia Dei, aut providentia ejus? Hanc rationem tangit Salomon in Ecclesiaste, ubi ait : Peccator ex eo quod centies peccat, et per patientiam sustentatur, ego cognovi quod erit bonum timentibus Deum, qui quærunt faciem ejus. De qua re subtilissime fatur, disputatque Psalmista, dicendo : Dixerunt, Quomodo scit Deus? et, Si est scientia in Excelso? Ecce ipsi peccatores et abundantes in sæculo obtinuerunt divitias. Deinde subdit in persona viri justi fidelis : Et dixi, Ergo sine causa justificavi cor meum, et lavi inter innocentes manus meas. Tanquam dicat : Si iniqui sic prosperabuntur, nec judicabuntur a Deo, ergo inaniter juste innocenterque vixi. Quod quam absurdum sit dicere, innuit subdens : Si dicebam, Narrabo sic : ecce nationem filiorum tuorum reprobavi, etc. Et alia multa profunda addit de isto ibidem.
paras.en: Finally, from these things a clear argument is drawn for the truth of the Christian faith. For we see the worst of men enjoy health and prosperity even to old age, while God-fearing, just and most devout men are at all times exercised by tribulations and adversities. If, then, there is no other life after the present one, in which a just retribution may be made, where is the justice of God, or his providence? Solomon touches on this reasoning in Ecclesiastes, where he says: [[Eccles 8:12|a sinner do evil a hundred times, and by patience be borne withal, I know from thence that it shall be well with them that fear God, who dread his face|Peccator ex eo quod centies peccat, et per patientiam sustentatur, ego cognovi quod erit bonum timentibus Deum, qui quærunt faciem ejus]] [Denis reads *qui quærunt faciem ejus*, who seek his face, where the Vulgate has *qui verentur*, who dread]. The Psalmist speaks and argues most subtly of this matter, saying: They said, [[Ps 72:11|How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?|Quomodo scit Deus? et, Si est scientia in Excelso?]] [[Ps 72:12|Behold these are sinners; and yet, abounding in the world they have obtained riches|Ecce ipsi peccatores et abundantes in sæculo obtinuerunt divitias]]. Then he adds in the person of a just and faithful man: [[Ps 72:13|And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, and washed my hands among the innocent|Et dixi, Ergo sine causa justificavi cor meum, et lavi inter innocentes manus meas]]. As if to say: if the wicked are to prosper so, and not be judged by God, then I have lived justly and innocently in vain. How absurd it is to say this he hints when he adds: [[Ps 72:15|If I said: I will speak thus; behold I should condemn the generation of thy children|Si dicebam, Narrabo sic : ecce nationem filiorum tuorum reprobavi]], etc. And he adds many other profound things on this in the same place.

paras.t: Et si justus vix salvabitur, id est, difficulter ad salutem pertinget finaliter, quum arcta sit via salutis, atque per multas tribulationes oporteat nos salvari, difficile quoque sit perseverare usque in finem, hostiumque evadere laqueos, et vincere tentationes, quæ et in extremis acrius sæviunt: impius, id est infidelis, et peccator, id est malus Christianus, ubi parebunt? id est, quo modo a vultu Dei et a rigore sui judicii se abscondere poterunt? Parebunt utique in judicio a sinistris, sed in malum ipsorum, et mallent non apparere. Et statim in lacum projicientur tartareum, ubi manebunt in æternum absconditi. — Porro, ut asserit Beda, hanc sententiam princeps Apostolorum ex Proverbiis Salomonis, secundum antiquam translationem, accepit. Pro quo S. Hieronymus transtulit: Si justus in terra recipit, quanto magis impius et peccator? hoc est, si justus in præsenti vita affligitur, quanto magis iniqui qui hic non castigantur, nec emendantur, post vitam hanc damnabuntur?
paras.en: [[4:18|And if the just man shall scarcely be saved|Et si justus vix salvabitur]], that is, will reach salvation at the last only with difficulty, since the way of salvation is strait, and we must be saved through many tribulations, and it is hard too to persevere to the end, to escape the snares of the enemy and to overcome temptations, which rage more fiercely at the last: [[4:18|the ungodly|impius]], that is, the unbeliever, [[4:18|and the sinner|et peccator]], that is, the bad Christian, where shall they [[4:18|appear|ubi parebunt]]? that is, how will they be able to hide themselves from the face of God and from the rigour of his judgment? They will indeed appear at the judgment, on the left hand[[Matt 25:41||]], but to their own harm, and they would rather not appear. And at once they will be cast into the pit of hell, where they will remain hidden for ever. Further, as Bede asserts, the prince of the Apostles took this sentence from the Proverbs of Solomon according to the old translation; in place of which St. Jerome translated: [[Prov 11:31|If the just man receive in the earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner|Si justus in terra recipit, quanto magis impius et peccator?]]? [the old translation, following the Greek, read: If the just man is scarcely saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?] that is, if the just man is afflicted in the present life, how much more will the wicked, who are neither chastised nor amended here, be damned after this life?

paras.t: Verumtamen certum est justos usque in finem perseverantes salvari. Idcirco quod ait, Si justus vix salvabitur, accipi potest per modum hyperbolicæ locutionis, qua aliquid dicitur per excessum, ad designandum magnitudinem rei insolitam. Sicque per verba ista insinuatur quam difficile sit hominem mortalem salvari: non ex parte omnipotentis Dei, in cujus manu sunt omnium corda, et quocumque voluerit, vertit ea absque omni difficultate ex parte sua, quum infinitæ virtuti omnia sint æque facilia; sed ex humana fragilitate, et multitudine ac magnitudine impugnationum atque tentationum oritur difficultas. Et quamvis Deus in hominis salvatione præsupponit liberum arbitrium, quod non cogitur, non tamen ex parte Dei est difficultas, ut aliqui somniant: quoniam Deus omnipotens superfacile, quando vult, infundit gratiam quamdam, quæ omnem cordis duritiam obicemque repellit ac tollit, ut sanctus loquitur Augustinus, et Thomas in Summa contra gentiles allegat.
paras.en: Nevertheless it is certain that the just who persevere to the end are saved[[Matt 10:22||]] [the margin gives Matth. v, 22; the saying is at Matt 10:22]. Therefore what he says, [[4:18|if the just man shall scarcely be saved|Si justus vix salvabitur]], can be taken as a hyperbolic expression [that is, an exaggeration made on purpose], by which something is said by way of excess to signify the unusual greatness of a thing. And so these words suggest how hard it is for mortal man to be saved: not on the part of almighty God, in whose hand are the hearts of all, and whithersoever he will he turns them[[Prov 21:1||]] without any difficulty on his part, since to infinite power all things are equally easy; but the difficulty arises from human frailty, and from the number and greatness of assaults and temptations. And although God, in saving man, presupposes free will, which is not compelled, yet the difficulty is not on God's part, as some dream: for almighty God, when he wills, most easily pours in a certain grace which drives back and takes away all hardness of heart and every obstacle, as holy Augustine says and Thomas cites in the Summa contra Gentiles.

paras.t: Quum igitur justus vix salvetur, ob rigorem divini judicii, in quo quæ homini justa videntur, sæpe injusta reperiuntur, congrue subditur: Itaque et hi qui patiuntur secundum voluntatem Dei, id est, pro justitia patiuntur adversa pie, æquanimiter et constanter, secundum quod complacet Deo, vel etiam correptiones et correctiones pro suis peccatis modo libenter suscipiunt, fideli Creatori commendant animas suas, id est, se ipsos Deo humiliter fiducialiterque committunt, non præsumendo de propriis viribus aut meritis, sed Deo omne bonum attribuentes, cujus dona sunt merita nostra. Idcirco subjungitur: in benefactis, id est in virtuosis suis operibus, quæ cupiunt pie acceptari a Deo, in quo totam suam figunt fiduciam, ejus subventioni, conservationi, protectioni jugiter inhærentes. De quo ad Corinthios loquitur Paulus: Fidelis Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis, sed faciet etiam cum tentatione proventum. Dicitur autem Deus fidelis, a fidelitate quæ est pars justitiæ, quia fidelibus suis servat fidelitatem, prout in Scripturis testatur. Propter quod ait Propheta: Fidelis Deus in omnibus verbis suis. De quo in Deuteronomio scribitur: Deus fortis et fidelis, custodiens pactum et misericordiam diligentibus se. Non autem vocatur fidelis, a fide quæ est theologica virtus, quæ ei non convenit.
paras.en: Since, then, the just man is scarcely saved, because of the rigour of the divine judgment, in which what seems just to man is often found unjust, it is fittingly added: [[4:19|Wherefore let them also that suffer according to the will of God|Itaque et hi qui patiuntur secundum voluntatem Dei]], that is, who suffer adversity for justice piously, with equanimity and constancy, as is pleasing to God, or who also now willingly accept rebukes and corrections for their sins, [[4:19|commend their souls|commendant animas suas]] [[4:19|to the faithful Creator|fideli Creatori]], that is, commit themselves humbly and trustfully to God, not presuming on their own strength or merits, but ascribing every good to God, whose gifts our merits are. Therefore it is added: [[4:19|in good deeds|in benefactis]], that is, in their virtuous works, which they desire to be graciously accepted by God, in whom they fix all their trust, cleaving constantly to his help, keeping and protection. Of whom Paul speaks to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 10:13|God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that which you are able: but will make also with temptation issue|Fidelis Deus, qui non patietur vos tentari supra id quod potestis, sed faciet etiam cum tentatione proventum]]. Now God is called faithful from fidelity, which is a part of justice, because he keeps faith with his faithful, as he testifies in the Scriptures. For which reason the Prophet says: [[Ps 144:13|The Lord is faithful in all his words|Fidelis Deus in omnibus verbis suis]]. Of whom it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 7:9|a strong and faithful God, keeping his covenant and mercy to them that love him|Deus fortis et fidelis, custodiens pactum et misericordiam diligentibus se]]. But he is not called faithful from faith, which is a theological virtue, for that does not befit him.

5.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI QUINTI : SENIORES ERGO QUI IN VOBIS SUNT.
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: The ancients therefore that are among you.

paras.t: INTRODUCTIS documentis ac jussionibus, ad quosdam specialiter pertinentibus, scilicet ad conjugatos ac servos, nunc specialiter instruit prælatos ac subditos.
paras.en: Having set out teachings and commands that belong to certain people in particular, namely to the married and to servants, he now instructs prelates and subjects in particular.

paras.t: Seniores ergo qui in vobis sunt, id est majores, videlicet prælatos et aliorum instructores, sive presbyteros: qui in primitiva Ecclesia communiter etiam corporali ætate fuerant seniores; obsecro, consenior, quia officio et senio consors, et testis Christi passionum, id est testificator suppliciorum quæ pro nobis sustinuit Christus: quæ partim propriis oculis vidi, idcirco de eis possum testari. Hinc ait Christus Apostolis: Vos testimonium perhibebitis, quia ab initio mecum estis. Et ejus, quæ in futuro revelanda est, gloriæ communicator, id est annuntiator seu prædicator felicitatis ac gloriæ sempiternæ, in futuro sæculo electis propalandæ et dandæ: quam instrumentaliter vobis communico, ad ejus adeptionem vobis cooperando meis prædicationibus, orationibus, meritis et exemplis. Vel dicitur sanctissimus Petrus communicator gloriæ Christi, quia in monte Thabor interfuit transfigurationi ipsius, in qua vultus Christi instar solis resplenduit, et qualis nunc est in cœlo empyreo, qualis etiam apparebit in judicio, demonstravit. Vidit quoque Christum post resurrectionem, et ascendentem in cœlum conspexit.
paras.en: [[5:1|The ancients therefore that are among you|Seniores ergo qui in vobis sunt]], that is, the elders, namely prelates and those who instruct others, or priests [Latin *presbyteros*, literally "elders"], who in the primitive Church were commonly elders in bodily age as well; [[5:1|I beseech|obsecro]], [[5:1|who am myself also an ancient|consenior]], because I share with them in office and in age, [[5:1|and a witness of the sufferings of Christ|et testis Christi passionum]], that is, one who bears witness to the torments which Christ endured for us: which I partly saw with my own eyes, and therefore I can bear witness to them. Hence Christ says to the Apostles: [[John 15:27|you shall give testimony, because you are with me from the beginning|Vos testimonium perhibebitis, quia ab initio mecum estis]]. [[5:1|as also a partaker of that glory which is to be revealed in time to come|Et ejus, quæ in futuro revelanda est, gloriæ communicator]] [Latin *communicator*, one who shares in a thing or imparts it to others], that is, the herald or preacher of the happiness and everlasting glory that is to be made known and given to the elect in the world to come: which I impart to you as an instrument, working with you towards gaining it by my preaching, prayers, merits and example. Or the most holy Peter is called a partaker of the glory of Christ because on Mount Thabor he was present at His transfiguration, in which the face of Christ shone like the sun, and showed what it now is in the empyrean heaven, and what it will also appear at the judgment. He also saw Christ after the resurrection, and beheld Him ascending into heaven.

paras.t: Pascite qui in vobis est gregem Dei: id est, unusquisque vestrum plebem sibi commissam diligenter spiritualibus alimoniis nutriat, utpote sapientia quæ est cognitio divinorum, et scientia quæ est rerum notitia creatarum, vel morali peritia. Pascenda est quoque plebs virtutum exemplis, fama laudabili, oratione assidua, prædicatione continua, ecclesiasticis sacramentis. De talibus pastoribus loquitur Dominus per Jeremiam: Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum; et pascent vos scientia et doctrina. Paulus quoque in Actibus episcopis loquitur: Attendite vobis et universo gregi in quo vos Spiritus Sanctus posuit episcopos, regere Ecclesiam. Præterea dulce fuit in ore sanctissimi Petri verbum hoc, Pascite, quoniam Christus dixerat ei: Pasce agnos meos. Et sicut Christus præfecit Petrum universali Ecclesiæ et populo universo, sic Petrus fuit sollicitus pro totius salute Ecclesiæ, hortando tum inferiores, tum prælatos, ut unusquisque digne exsequatur suum officium.
paras.en: [[5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you|Pascite qui in vobis est gregem Dei]]: that is, let each of you diligently nourish the people committed to him with spiritual food, namely with wisdom, which is the knowledge of divine things, and with knowledge [*scientia*], which is the acquaintance with created things, or with skill in morals. The people must also be fed with examples of virtue, with a praiseworthy name, with constant prayer, with continual preaching, and with the sacraments of the Church. Of such pastors the Lord speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 3:15|I will give you pastors according to my own heart, and they shall feed you with knowledge and doctrine|Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum; et pascent vos scientia et doctrina]]. Paul too, in the Acts, says to the bishops: [[Acts 20:28|Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock, wherein the Holy Ghost hath placed you bishops, to rule the Church|Attendite vobis et universo gregi in quo vos Spiritus Sanctus posuit episcopos, regere Ecclesiam]]. Moreover, this word [[5:2|Feed|Pascite]] was sweet in the mouth of the most holy Peter, since Christ had said to him: [[John 21:15|Feed my lambs|Pasce agnos meos]]. And as Christ set Peter over the universal Church and the whole people, so Peter was solicitous for the salvation of the whole Church, exhorting both those below and the prelates, that each should worthily carry out his office.

paras.t: Providentes, id est salubria procurantes subditis vestris, et provide vos habentes ad illos, futura pericula præcavendo pro posse, non coacte, sed spontanee, id est caritative et libere, non ex necessitate, aut sola indigentia rei terrenæ. Coacte enim hæc agit, qui aliunde non habens quo sustentetur, propter temporale commodum dumtaxat populo prædicat, ac spiritualia alimenta impendit. Hinc loquitur Paulus: Si volens hoc ago, mercedem habeo; si autem invitus, dispensatio mihi credita est. Providendum est ergo spontanee, secundum Deum, id est recta intentione ad Dei honorem propter vestram ac subditorum salutem. Neque turpis lucri gratia, non intuitu proprii quæstus, sed voluntarie, propter commodum spirituale. Neque ut dominantes in clero, id est non ex fastu superbiæ, sed ex humilitate. Nempe prælati qui ex consideratione suæ dignitatis seu præsidentiæ extolluntur, et pompatice jubent, atque faciliter indignantur, ac subditos spernunt, hi tales sunt ut dominantes in clero: qui magis proprium quam Dei honorem respiciunt, nec curant de Dei inhonoratione, dummodo ipsi a subditis honorentur. Non enim habent sincerum zelum justitiæ, sed ad se ipsos vitiose reflexi sunt. Et istud prohibuit Christus in Cœna novissima, quia apud Lucam habetur: Quum facta fuisset inter discipulos contentio, quis eorum videretur esse major, respondit Salvator: Reges gentium dominantur eorum, vos autem non sic; sed qui major est in vobis, fiat sicut junior, et qui præcessor est, sicut ministrator.
paras.en: [[5:2|taking care of it|Providentes]], that is, procuring wholesome things for your subjects and bearing yourselves providently towards them, guarding as far as you can against dangers to come, [[5:2|not by constraint but willingly|non coacte, sed spontanee]], that is, out of charity and freely, not from necessity or from mere want of earthly goods. For he does this by constraint who, having nothing else to live on, preaches to the people and bestows spiritual food on them only for temporal gain. Hence Paul says: [[1 Cor 9:17|if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward: but if against my will, a dispensation is committed to me|Si volens hoc ago, mercedem habeo; si autem invitus, dispensatio mihi credita est]]. Care must be taken willingly, then, [[5:2|according to God|secundum Deum]], that is, with right intention, for the honour of God, for the sake of your own salvation and your subjects'. [[5:2|not for filthy lucre's sake|Neque turpis lucri gratia]], not with an eye to your own gain, [[5:2|but voluntarily|sed voluntarie]], for spiritual profit. [[5:3|Neither as lording it over the clergy|Neque ut dominantes in clero]], that is, not out of proud arrogance, but out of humility. For prelates who are puffed up by the thought of their dignity or authority, who give orders pompously, are easily angered and despise their subjects, these are such as lord it over the clergy: they look to their own honour rather than God's, and care nothing for the dishonour done to God, so long as they themselves are honoured by their subjects. For they have no sincere zeal for justice, but are viciously turned back upon themselves. And this Christ forbade at the Last Supper, for it is found in Luke: When there had been a strife among the disciples, [[Luke 22:24|which of them should seem to be the greater|quis eorum videretur esse major]], the Saviour answered: [[Luke 22:25|The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them|Reges gentium dominantur eorum]]; [[Luke 22:26|But you not so: but he that is the greater among you, let him become as the younger: and he that is the leader, as he that serveth|vos autem non sic; sed qui major est in vobis, fiat sicut junior, et qui præcessor est, sicut ministrator]].

paras.t: Denique duplex est dominium: Unum ordinatum, videlicet dignitas principatus, sive prælatio ad inferiorum profectum relata. Et istud dominium competit præsidentibus, sicque domini possunt vocari. Unde et Josue dixit: Domine mi Moyses, prohibe eos; et Aaron ad Moysen, Ne indignetur, inquit, dominus meus: cui et tribus Ruben et Gad loquebantur, Servi tui sumus. Sic et S. Clemens vocavit beatissimum Petrum dominum suum, ut in Itinerario Clementis habetur. Et filii Israel dixerunt ad Gedeonem: Dominare tu nostri. In Actibus quoque Apostolorum custos carceris dixit Paulo atque Silæ: Domini, quid me oportet facere, ut salvus fiam? Sic et Anselmus in epistola de incarnatione Verbi, scribit Romano Pontifici: Domino et patri universæ Ecclesiæ peregrinantis in terra. — Aliud est dominium inordinatum, utpote præsidentia ad proprium commodum ex fastu relata: quæ prælatis atque principibus prohibetur, quum in Deuteronomio Dominus dicat de rege: Non elevetur cor ejus in superbiam super fratres suos, neque declinet in partem dexteram vel sinistram. In Ecclesiastico quoque habetur: Rectorem te posuerunt? Noli extolli; esto in illis quasi unus ex eis; curam illorum habe, et ita considera. De hac re multa scribit Bernardus in libro de Consideratione. — Per hanc quoque distinctionem multa verba Sanctorum ad invicem concordantur, quæ inter se repugnantiam quamdam habere videntur.
paras.en: Further, lordship is of two kinds. The one is ordered, namely the dignity of rule, or prelacy directed to the advancement of those below. And this lordship belongs to those who preside, and so they may be called lords. Hence Josue said: [[Num 11:28|My lord Moses forbid them|Domine mi Moyses, prohibe eos]]; and Aaron to Moses: [[Ex 32:22|Let not|Ne indignetur]], he says, [[Ex 32:22|my lord be offended|dominus meus]]; to whom also the tribes of Ruben and Gad said: [[Num 32:25|We are thy servants|Servi tui sumus]]. So too St. Clement called the most blessed Peter his lord, as is found in the *Itinerary* of Clement [the *Recognitions* ascribed to St. Clement of Rome]. And the children of Israel said to Gedeon: [[Judg 8:22|Rule thou over us|Dominare tu nostri]]. In the Acts of the Apostles, too, the keeper of the prison said to Paul and Silas: [[Acts 16:30|Masters, what must I do, that I may be saved?|Domini, quid me oportet facere, ut salvus fiam?]] [in the Latin, *Domini*, "lords"] So too Anselm, in his letter on the Incarnation of the Word, writes to the Roman Pontiff: To the lord and father of the universal Church on pilgrimage on earth. — The other is disordered lordship, namely authority directed to one's own advantage out of pride: this is forbidden to prelates and princes, since in Deuteronomy the Lord says of the king: [[Deut 17:20|And that his heart be not lifted up with pride over his brethren, nor decline to the right or to the left|Non elevetur cor ejus in superbiam super fratres suos, neque declinet in partem dexteram vel sinistram]]. In Ecclesiasticus too it is found: [[Ecclus 32:1|Have they made thee ruler? be not lifted up: be among them as one of them|Rectorem te posuerunt? Noli extolli; esto in illis quasi unus ex eis]]; [[Ecclus 32:2|Have care of them|curam illorum habe]], and so consider [Denis reads *considera*, "consider", where the Vulgate has *conside*, "sit down"]. Of this Bernard writes much in his book *On Consideration*. — By this distinction, too, many sayings of the Saints that seem somewhat at odds with one another are brought into agreement.

paras.t: Præterea, quia ordinatum dominium, et recta prælatio, non ad proprium commodum seu honorem, sed ad subditorum utilitatem refertur, idcirco prælationes et dignitates ecclesiasticæ, servitutes vocantur; et ipsi qui præsunt, servos se veraciter reputant eorum qui suæ gubernationi commissi sunt. Unde et Pontifex summus appellat se servum servorum Dei. Propterea prælati et principes debent tanto humiliores, timoratiores et custoditiores consistere, quanto pluribus præsident, utpote districtius judicandi, atque pro pluribus rationem daturi.
paras.en: Moreover, because ordered lordship and right prelacy are directed not to one's own advantage or honour but to the good of one's subjects, therefore ecclesiastical prelacies and dignities are called services [Latin *servitutes*, literally "servitudes"]; and those who preside truly reckon themselves the servants of those committed to their government. Hence the supreme Pontiff calls himself the servant of the servants of God. Therefore prelates and princes ought to be the more humble, the more God-fearing and the more watchful over themselves, the more people they preside over, since they are to be judged more strictly and are to render an account for more.

paras.t: Sed forma facti gregis, id est gregi vobis credito exemplares effecti. Nempe, quum unusquisque debeat proximorum scandala devitare, eosque ædificare, dicente Apostolo, Quæ ædificationis sunt, invicem custodiamus; et item, Hoc judicate, ne ponatis fratri offendiculum vel scandalum: multo magis ista ad prælatos superioresque pertinent, qui ex officio specialiter obligantur subditos a vitiis expurgare, et ad virtutes inducere. Propter quod Timotheo antistiti præcipit Paulus: Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate; et rursus: Sollicite cura te ipsum probabilem exhibere Deo, operarium inconfusibilem, recte tractantem verbum veritatis. Tito quoque archiepiscopo scribens: In omnibus, inquit, te ipsum præbe exemplum bonorum operum, in doctrina, in integritate, in gravitate. Teste quippe Gregorio: Quum pastor per abrupta graditur, grex ejus in præcipitium labitur; et cujus vita despicitur, restat ut ejus prædicatio contemnatur. Ex virtuosa siquidem et exemplari conversatione ac informatione superiorum, in tantum dependent profectus et salus inferiorum, ut per Jeremiam Dominus protestetur: Quoniam stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt, propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. In Ecclesiastico etiam dicitur: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea. Væ ergo, et væ æternum atque gravissimum præsidentibus, vitam carnalem, negligentem, scandalosam ducentibus, quoniam universa subditorum peccata in eos redundant.
paras.en: [[5:3|but being made a pattern of the flock|Sed forma facti gregis]], that is, made examples to the flock entrusted to you. For since each one ought to avoid giving scandal to his neighbours, and ought to edify them, as the Apostle says, [[Rom 14:19|keep the things that are of edification, one towards another|Quæ ædificationis sunt, invicem custodiamus]], and again, [[Rom 14:13|judge this rather, that you put not a stumblingblock or a scandal in your brother's way|Hoc judicate, ne ponatis fratri offendiculum vel scandalum]]: much more do these things belong to prelates and superiors, who are bound in particular by their office to purge their subjects of vices and to lead them to virtues. For this reason Paul commands Timothy, a bishop: [[1 Tim 4:12|be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity|Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate]]; and again: [[2 Tim 2:15|Carefully study to present thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.|Sollicite cura te ipsum probabilem exhibere Deo, operarium inconfusibilem, recte tractantem verbum veritatis]] Writing also to the archbishop Titus: [[Tit 2:7|In all things|In omnibus]], he says, [[Tit 2:7|shew thyself an example of good works, in doctrine, in integrity, in gravity|te ipsum præbe exemplum bonorum operum, in doctrina, in integritate, in gravitate]]. For, as Gregory witnesses: When the shepherd walks over steep places, his flock slips down to the precipice; and when a man's life is despised, it follows that his preaching is scorned. For the progress and salvation of those below depend so much on the virtuous and exemplary life and teaching of their superiors that the Lord declares through Jeremias: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly, and have not sought the Lord|Quoniam stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt]]: therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiii, 1; the words are those of Jer 10:21]. In Ecclesiasticus too it is said: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers: and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein.|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus; et qualis est rector civitatis, tales et inhabitantes in ea]] Woe, then, and woe eternal and most grievous to those who preside and lead a carnal, negligent, scandalous life, since all the sins of their subjects redound upon them.

paras.t: Et ex animo, id est, integro corde, prompto affectu, recta intentione, firmo proposito, pastorale officium adimplete, cum omni diligentia et fervore, quum hi vobis commissi sint pro quibus sanguinem suum Dei Filius fudit, qui his quorum negligentiis et vitiis tam pretiosissime a se redemptos amisit, implacabiliter et supergravissime irascetur, juxta illud Sapientiæ: Cito et horrende apparebit vobis Altissimus, qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur.
paras.en: [[5:3|from the heart|Et ex animo]], that is, with an undivided heart, ready affection, right intention and firm purpose, fulfil the pastoral office with all diligence and fervour, since those committed to you are they for whom the Son of God shed His blood; and He will be implacably and most grievously angry with those through whose negligence and vices He has lost those whom He redeemed at so very great a price, according to that word of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:6|Horribly and speedily will he appear to you|Cito et horrende apparebit vobis]], the Most High, [[Wis 6:4|who will examine your works: and search out your thoughts|qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur]].

paras.t: Et quum apparuerit princeps pastorum, videlicet Christus, qui est princeps pastorum supremus et principalis. Romanus vero Pontifex, est princeps pastorum et totius universalis militantis Ecclesiæ prælatus ac præsul vicarialis. Percipietis immarcescibilem gloriæ coronam, id est æternam et indeficientem felicitatis remunerationem, beatitudinis bravium, salutis triumphum. Apparebit autem Christus, non solum in finali judicio, sed in particulari quoque judicio singulorum, quos suo sisti præcipit tribunali. Propter quod ait: Vigilate, quia nescitis diem neque horam. Quemadmodum autem gravissima est negligentium carnaliumque pastorum damnatio; sic fidelium, diligentium, exemplariumque præsidentium copiosissima erit felicitas, et præmium inæstimabiliter gloriosum: quia non solum pro suis actibus virtuosis, sed pro subditorum etiam meritis coronabuntur. Propter quod ad Thessalonicenses loquitur Paulus: Quæ est enim spes nostra, aut gaudium, aut corona gloriæ? nonne vos ante Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, in adventu ejus?
paras.en: [[5:4|And when the prince of pastors shall appear|Et quum apparuerit princeps pastorum]], namely Christ, who is the supreme and principal prince of pastors. The Roman Pontiff, however, is prince of pastors, and prelate and vicarial head [that is, head as Christ's vicar] of the whole universal Church militant. [[5:4|you shall receive a never fading crown of glory|Percipietis immarcescibilem gloriæ coronam]], that is, the eternal and unfailing reward of happiness, the prize [Latin *bravium*, the prize of a race] of beatitude, the triumph of salvation. And Christ will appear not only at the last judgment, but also at the particular judgment of each one, whom He commands to be set before His tribunal. For this reason He says: [[Matt 25:13|Watch ye|Vigilate]], [[Matt 25:13|because you know not the day nor the hour|quia nescitis diem neque horam]]. And as the damnation of negligent and carnal pastors is most grievous, so the happiness of faithful, diligent and exemplary superiors will be most abundant, and their reward glorious beyond reckoning: for they will be crowned not only for their own virtuous acts, but also for the merits of their subjects. For this reason Paul says to the Thessalonians: [[1 Thess 2:19|For what is our hope or joy or crown of glory? Are not you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?|Quæ est enim spes nostra, aut gaudium, aut corona gloriæ? nonne vos ante Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, in adventu ejus?]]

paras.t: Similiter, adolescentes, subditi estote senioribus, id est, superioribus vestris obedite, quomodo eis præcepi vobis præesse, videlicet non coacte, sed spontanee, secundum Deum, sincera intentione et ex animo, quemadmodum ad Hebræos dicitur: Obedite præpositis vestris, et subjacete eis: ipsi enim pervigilant quasi rationem reddituri pro animabus vestris, ut cum gaudio hoc faciant, et non gementes. Subditi itaque circa suos superiores habere se debent reverenter, obedienter, pacifice et amorose. Hinc ad Thessalonicenses loquitur Paulus: Rogamus vos, fratres, ut noveritis eos qui laborant inter vos, et præsunt vobis in Domino, et monent vos, ut habeatis illos abundantius in caritate propter opus illorum; et pacem habete cum eis. Etenim, quam salubre sit superioribus obedire, quam item damnabile sit eis non obedire, Christus breviter pandit, dicendo suis vicariis, utpote his qui præsunt: Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit. Nec solum senioribus præsidentibus, sed et omnibus senioribus aliquis honor debetur. Propter quod in Levitico scriptum est: Coram cano capite consurge, et honora personam senis; et in Ecclesiastico habetur, In multitudine presbyterorum prudentium sta, et sapientiæ illorum ex corde conjungere. In antiquis namque est sapientia, et in multo tempore prudentia, ut in libro Job fertur.
paras.en: [[5:5|In like manner, ye young men, be subject to the ancients|Similiter, adolescentes, subditi estote senioribus]], that is, obey your superiors in the way in which I have commanded them to be over you, namely [[5:2|not by constraint but willingly|non coacte, sed spontanee]], [[5:2|according to God|secundum Deum]], with sincere intention and [[5:3|from the heart|ex animo]]; as is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:17|Obey your prelates and be subject to them. For they watch as being to render an account of your souls: that they may do this with joy and not with grief|Obedite præpositis vestris, et subjacete eis: ipsi enim pervigilant quasi rationem reddituri pro animabus vestris, ut cum gaudio hoc faciant, et non gementes]]. Subjects, then, ought to bear themselves towards their superiors with reverence, obedience, peace and love. Hence Paul says to the Thessalonians: [[1 Thess 5:12|we beseech you, brethren, to know them who labour among you and are over you in the Lord and admonish you|Rogamus vos, fratres, ut noveritis eos qui laborant inter vos, et præsunt vobis in Domino, et monent vos]]; [[1 Thess 5:13|That you esteem them more abundantly in charity, for their work's sake. Have peace with them|ut habeatis illos abundantius in caritate propter opus illorum; et pacem habete cum eis]]. Indeed, how wholesome it is to obey superiors, and again how damnable not to obey them, Christ briefly shows, saying to His vicars, that is, to those who preside: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]]. And not only to the elders who preside, but to all the aged some honour is due. For this reason it is written in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:32|Rise up before the hoary head, and honour the person of the aged man|Coram cano capite consurge, et honora personam senis]]; and in Ecclesiasticus it is found: [[Ecclus 6:35|Stand in the multitude of ancients that are wise, and join thyself from thy heart to their wisdom|In multitudine presbyterorum prudentium sta, et sapientiæ illorum ex corde conjungere]]. For [[Job 12:12|In the ancient is wisdom, and in length of days prudence|In antiquis namque est sapientia, et in multo tempore prudentia]], as is said in the book of Job.

paras.t: Omnes autem invicem humilitatem insinuate, id est, unusquisque circa alterum se gerat humiliter. Nec subditi tantum humiliter pareant, sed prælati quoque humiliter præsint. Nec solum verbis, sed et exemplis in humilitate instruant sibi commissos, quum in Ecclesiastico scriptum sit: Quanto magnus es, humilia te in omnibus, et coram Deo invenies gratiam, quoniam ab humilibus honoratur. Et Christus testatur: Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, id est humiles, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum. Subditi ergo circa superiores suos, tanquam circa Dei vicarios, suos patres, judices ac dominos, humilitatem demonstrent. Superiores vero circa inferiores, tanquam circa Christi membra, adoptionisque Dei filios, Christi sanguine liberatos, summæ Trinitatis imagine insignitos, se humiliter habeant. Denique, quamvis prælatus sit major ecclesiastica dignitate, pie tamen putare habet quod subditi sui, vel saltem quidam eorum, majores sint eo caritate et gratia ac perfectione virtutum: quod multo salubrius est. Ideo circa eos se humiliter gerat, et se eis viliorem arbitretur, salvo tamen disciplinæ vigore ac strenua pastoralis officii exsecutione. Hinc loquitur Paulus: Honore invicem prævenientes; et denuo, Per humilitatem sibi invicem superiores arbitrantes. Quia Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam: quod super Jacobi Canonicam expositum est. Et est verbum hoc omnibus nobis semper valde pensandum, quum tanti sit ponderis ut tam princeps Apostolorum, quam frater Domini Jacobus, illud in suis allegent epistolis. Quod quum ita sit, merito subditur:
paras.en: [[5:5|And do you all insinuate humility one to another|Omnes autem invicem humilitatem insinuate]] [Latin *insinuate*, bring in, commend], that is, let each bear himself humbly towards the other. Let not subjects only obey humbly, but let prelates also preside humbly. And let them instruct those committed to them in humility not only by words but also by example, since it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:20|The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things, and thou shalt find grace before God:|Quanto magnus es, humilia te in omnibus, et coram Deo invenies gratiam]] for [[Ecclus 3:21|he is honoured by the humble|ab humilibus honoratur]]. And Christ testifies: [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli]], that is, humble, [[Matt 18:3|you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]]. Subjects, then, should show humility towards their superiors as towards the vicars of God, their fathers, judges and lords. Superiors, for their part, should bear themselves humbly towards those below them as towards the members of Christ, the adopted sons of God, set free by the blood of Christ, marked with the image of the most high Trinity. Further, although a prelate be greater in ecclesiastical dignity, he ought nevertheless piously to think that his subjects, or at least some of them, are greater than he in charity and grace and perfection of virtues: which is much more wholesome. Let him therefore bear himself humbly towards them and judge himself lower than they, yet without loss of the vigour of discipline and of the energetic carrying out of the pastoral office. Hence Paul says: [[Rom 12:10|with honour preventing one another|Honore invicem prævenientes]] [*preventing*, that is, going before]; and again, [[Phil 2:3|in humility, let each esteem others better than themselves|Per humilitatem sibi invicem superiores arbitrantes]]; [[5:5|for God resisteth the proud, but to the humble he giveth grace|Quia Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam]][[Jas 4:6||]]: which has been expounded on the Canonical Epistle of James. And this word must always be weighed well by all of us, since it is of such weight that both the prince of the Apostles and James the brother of the Lord set it down in their epistles. This being so, there follows fittingly:

paras.t: Humiliamini igitur sub potenti manu Dei, id est, sub omnipotente Deo, cui nullus valet resistere, humiliter incedite, defectuositates vestras perpendite, in eo confidite, ejus misericordiam jugiter implorate, ei in omni humilitate servite, omnem arrogantiæ tumorem jugiter abhorrentes, ut vos exaltet, id est, in regno æternæ beatitudinis collocet, in tempore visitationis, id est in hora judicii vestri particularis, quantum ad animam; in hora quoque universalis judicii, quoad corpus et animam. Sicque exaltatio ista loco et dignitate, statu et gradu excellentior est, quum fiat de terra super cœlos, de imperfectione ad perfectionem, de mortalitate ad immortalitatem, de peregrinatione et exsilio ad felicitatem ac patriam. Hinc ait Salvator: Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur; et qui se exaltat, humiliabitur. Quod etiam in Proverbiis expressit Salomon, loquens: Superbum sequitur humilitas, et humilem spiritu suscipiet gloria. Unde et rursus in Proverbiis contestatur: Gloriam præcedit humilitas. In Job quoque asseritur: Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria.
paras.en: [[5:6|Be you humbled therefore under the mighty hand of God|Humiliamini igitur sub potenti manu Dei]], that is, under almighty God, whom no one can resist[[Esth 13:9||]]: walk humbly, weigh your failings, trust in Him, implore His mercy unceasingly, serve Him in all humility, abhorring at all times every swelling of arrogance, [[5:6|that he may exalt you|ut vos exaltet]], that is, set you in the kingdom of eternal beatitude, [[5:6|in the time of visitation|in tempore visitationis]], that is, in the hour of your particular judgment, as regards the soul; and also in the hour of the universal judgment, as regards body and soul. And so this exaltation is the more excellent in place and dignity, in state and degree, since it is from earth to above the heavens, from imperfection to perfection, from mortality to immortality, from pilgrimage and exile to happiness and the fatherland. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 14:11|he that humbleth himself shall be exalted|Qui se humiliat, exaltabitur]]; and [[Luke 14:11|every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled|qui se exaltat, humiliabitur]][[Luke 18:14||]]. This Solomon also expressed in Proverbs, saying: [[Prov 29:23|Humiliation followeth the proud: and glory shall uphold the humble of spirit.|Superbum sequitur humilitas, et humilem spiritu suscipiet gloria]] Hence again in Proverbs he declares: [[Prov 15:33|humility goeth before glory|Gloriam præcedit humilitas]]. In Job too it is affirmed: [[Job 22:29|he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory|Qui humiliatus fuerit, erit in gloria]].

paras.t: Omnem sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in eum, id est Deo committentes, quoniam ipsi cura, id est providentia, est de vobis. Hoc sumptum videtur ex illo Psalmistæ versiculo: Jacta super Dominum curam tuam, et ipse te enutriet. Hoc est quod ait Salvator: Nolite solliciti esse, dicentes, Quid manducabimus, aut quid bibemus, aut quo operiemur? Scit enim Pater vester cœlestis, quia his omnibus indigetis. Quærite ergo primum regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis. Unde et Paulus: Nihil, ait, solliciti sitis.
paras.en: [[5:7|Casting all your care upon him|Omnem sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in eum]], that is, committing it to God, [[5:7|for he hath care|quoniam ipsi cura]], that is, providence, [[5:7|of you|est de vobis]]. This seems to be taken from that verse of the Psalmist: [[Ps 54:23|Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee|Jacta super Dominum curam tuam, et ipse te enutriet]]. This is what the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:31|Be not solicitous therefore, saying: What shall we eat: or what shall we drink, or wherewith shall we be clothed?|Nolite solliciti esse, dicentes, Quid manducabimus, aut quid bibemus, aut quo operiemur?]] [[Matt 6:32|For your Father knoweth that you have need of all these things|Scit enim Pater vester cœlestis, quia his omnibus indigetis]] [Denis adds *cœlestis*, "heavenly"]. [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you.|Quærite ergo primum regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et hæc omnia adjicientur vobis]] Hence Paul too: [[Phil 4:6|Be nothing|Nihil]], he says, [[Phil 4:6|solicitous|solliciti sitis]].

paras.t: Verumtamen ita non sunt hæc intelligenda, quasi homo debeat negligere sive omittere quod in se est, quum hoc esset Deum tentare; sed ideo dicta sunt, ut in Deo quasi in piissimo ac sapientissimo patre ac domino confidamus, atque per ejus opem ac providentiam necessaria vitæ consequi nunc speremus, non immoderatam, sed moderatam curam, conatum et diligentiam apponentes. Quæ cura dicitur moderata, quando non est mentis perturbativa, angustiativa ac impeditiva devotionis. Immoderata vero, ex opposito prohibetur. Immoderata enim sollicitudo, diffidentiæ filia est, quoniam venit ex hoc quod homo non satis confidit in Deo, nec providentiæ ejus innititur. Denique duplex est sollicitudo, videlicet: spiritualis, quæ est pro vitiis repellendis virtutibusque adipiscendis. Quæ commendatur, juxta illud Deuteronomii: Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite: et illud Michææ: Indicabo tibi quid sit bonum: utique sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo. Alia est sollicitudo temporalis, quæ est circa terrena acquirenda aut conservanda seu dispensanda. Et ista est duplex, ut tactum est, utpote: moderata, de qua loquitur Paulus, Sollicitus fui hoc ipsum facere, puta, eleemosynas congregare pro sanctis pauperibus qui in Jerusalem erant; et immoderata, de qua in Proverbiis legitur, Expectatio sollicitorum peribit. Est demum specialiter Deo cura seu providentia de hominibus, præsertim fidelibus, et maxime de electis: quorum quilibet dicere potest Deo, Tenuisti manum dexteram meam, et in voluntate tua deduxisti me.
paras.en: Yet these things are not to be understood as though a man ought to neglect or leave undone what lies in his power, since that would be to tempt God; but they were said so that we may trust in God as in a most loving and most wise father and lord, and may hope now to obtain the necessities of life through His help and providence, applying care, effort and diligence that is not immoderate but moderate. That care is called moderate which does not disturb or straiten the mind, nor hinder devotion. Immoderate care, on the contrary, is forbidden. For immoderate solicitude is the daughter of distrust, since it comes from this, that a man does not trust enough in God nor rely on His providence. Further, solicitude is of two kinds. The one is spiritual, which is for driving out vices and gaining virtues. This is commended, according to that word of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]], and that of Micheas: [[Mich 6:8|I will shew thee, O man, what is good|Indicabo tibi quid sit bonum]]: verily [[Mich 6:8|to walk solicitous with thy God|sollicitum ambulare cum Deo tuo]]. The other is temporal solicitude, which is about acquiring, keeping or dispensing earthly things. And this, as has been touched on, is of two kinds: moderate, of which Paul speaks, [[Gal 2:10|which same thing also I was careful to do|Sollicitus fui hoc ipsum facere]] [in the Latin, *Sollicitus fui*, "I was solicitous"], namely, to collect alms for the holy poor who were in Jerusalem; and immoderate, of which we read in Proverbs, [[Prov 11:7|the expectation of the solicitous shall perish|Expectatio sollicitorum peribit]]. Lastly, God has a special care or providence for men, especially for the faithful, and most of all for the elect, any of whom can say to God: [[Ps 72:24|Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me|Tenuisti manum dexteram meam, et in voluntate tua deduxisti me]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxx, 24; the verse is Ps 72:24].

paras.t: Sobrii estote, in cibo, potu, somno, et ceteris corporis necessariis moderamen servantes, sicut ait Salvator: Non graventur corda vestra crapula, vel ebrietate, aut curis hujus sæculi. Qui iterum ait: Væ vobis qui saturati estis. Et vigilate, id est, virtuosis operibus diligenter intenti sitis. Non enim dormientibus, et otio desidiaque torpentibus, provenit regnum cœlorum, sed sollicite ambulantibus coram Deo. Imo maledictus qui facit opus Dei negligenter. Vigilandum est quoque, ut quantum rationabiliter fieri potest, abstrahamus nobis de somno, et paucas horas dormitioni indulgeamus, quatenus plus de tempore in virtuosis operibus expendamus, quum in Proverbiis Salomon dicat: Pigredo immittit soporem; et rursus, Sicut ostium vertitur in cardine suo, sic piger in lectulo; itemque, Usquequo, piger, dormies? In Ecclesiastico quoque habetur: Vigilia honestatis tabefaciet carnes, et cogitatus illius auferet somnum. Et certe vehementissima ac copiosissima ratio nobis est taliter vigilandi. Nam subditur: quia adversarius vester diabolus, qui est atrocissimus, implacabilis et infatigabilis hostis noster, tanquam leo rugiens, id est crudeliter, circuit homines (prout ait in libro Job: Circuivi terram et perambulavi eam), quærens quem devoret, id est, spiritualiter necet, et sibi incorporet, atque infernali ergastulo ingerat absorbendum. Dum enim ad mortale vitium pertrahit hominem, spiritualiter perimit eum, facitque eum membrum ac vernam suum.
paras.en: [[5:8|Be sober|Sobrii estote]], keeping measure in food, drink, sleep and the other necessities of the body, as the Saviour says: Let not [[Luke 21:34|your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness and the cares of this life|Non graventur corda vestra crapula, vel ebrietate, aut curis hujus sæculi]]. Who says again: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that are filled|Væ vobis qui saturati estis]]. [[5:8|and watch|Et vigilate]], that is, be diligently intent on virtuous works. For the kingdom of heaven does not come to those who sleep and grow torpid in idleness and sloth, but to those who walk solicitously before God. Nay, [[Jer 48:10|Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord|maledictus qui facit opus Dei]] negligently [the Vulgate has *fraudulenter*, "deceitfully", where Denis has *negligenter*]. We must watch also in this sense, that as far as can reasonably be done we take from our sleep and grant few hours to slumber, so as to spend more of our time in virtuous works, since Solomon says in Proverbs: [[Prov 19:15|Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep|Pigredo immittit soporem]]; and again, [[Prov 26:14|As the door turneth upon its hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.|Sicut ostium vertitur in cardine suo, sic piger in lectulo]] And again, [[Prov 6:9|How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard?|Usquequo, piger, dormies?]] In Ecclesiasticus too it is found: [[Ecclus 31:1|Watching for riches consumeth the flesh, and the thought thereof driveth away sleep.|Vigilia honestatis tabefaciet carnes, et cogitatus illius auferet somnum]] [Latin *Vigilia honestatis*, which Denis takes as the watching of virtue; the Douay-Rheims renders it "watching for riches"] And surely we have a most powerful and abundant reason to watch in this way. For there follows: [[5:8|because your adversary the devil|quia adversarius vester diabolus]], who is our most savage, implacable and tireless enemy, [[5:8|as a roaring lion|tanquam leo rugiens]], that is, cruelly, [[5:8|goeth about|circuit]] among men (as he says in the book of Job: [[Job 1:7|I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it|Circuivi terram et perambulavi eam]][[Job 2:2||]]), [[5:8|seeking whom he may devour|quærens quem devoret]], that is, to slay spiritually, to make part of himself, and to thrust into the prison of hell to be swallowed up. For when he draws a man into mortal sin, he slays him spiritually and makes him his member and his slave.

paras.t: Cui resistite fortes in fide. Fides namque est propugnaculum Christianorum contra universas insidias dæmonum. Propter quod ad Ephesios fertur: In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei, in quo possitis omnia tela nequissimi ignea exstinguere. Et in S. Joannis Canonica legitur: Hæc est victoria quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra. Fides namque est fundamentum virtutum, præcipuique vigoris, ac magni meriti apud Deum. Propter quod in Evangelio loquitur Christus: Secundum fidem vestram fiat vobis; et, Omnia possibilia sunt credenti; et, Fides tua te salvum fecit. Quæ de fide formata sunt accipienda. Insuper, diabolo resistere semper debemus, nos ipsos in omnibus humiliando, in Deo plenarie confidendo, et gratiosam adsistentiam indefesse rogando, dominicam passionem intime atque assidue revolvendo, considerando quoque quatuor novissima, et invocando Virginem gloriosam, angelos sanctos, et Sanctos ad quos majorem habemus devotionem, quilibet etiam angelum sui custodem. Scientes eamdem passionem ei quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitati fieri, id est, hoc cognoscentes, quod passio, tribulatio sive tentatio quæ vobis infligitur ab invisibilibus seu visibilibus hostibus, etiam ubique terrarum infligitur Christianis seu toti Ecclesiæ: quoniam omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patiuntur. Ideo non putetis vobis aliquid insolitum evenire: imo erubescite, si præ ceteris tentationibus tribulationibusque victi fueritis.
paras.en: [[5:9|Whom resist ye, strong in faith|Cui resistite fortes in fide]]. For faith is the bulwark of Christians against all the snares of the demons. For this reason it is said to the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:16|In all things taking the shield of faith, wherewith you may be able to extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one.|In omnibus sumentes scutum fidei, in quo possitis omnia tela nequissimi ignea exstinguere]] And in the Canonical Epistle of St. John we read: [[1 John 5:4|this is the victory which overcameth the world: Our faith|Hæc est victoria quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra]]. For faith is the foundation of the virtues, of chief strength and of great merit with God. For this reason Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 9:29|According to your faith, be it done unto you|Secundum fidem vestram fiat vobis]]; and, [[Mark 9:22|all things are possible to him that believeth|Omnia possibilia sunt credenti]]; and, [[Mark 10:52|Thy faith hath made thee whole|Fides tua te salvum fecit]][[Mark 5:34||]]. These are to be understood of formed faith [that is, faith quickened by charity]. Moreover, we must always resist the devil by humbling ourselves in all things, trusting fully in God and asking unweariedly for His gracious help, by turning over the Lord's passion inwardly and constantly, by considering also the four last things, and by calling upon the glorious Virgin, the holy angels and the Saints to whom we have the greater devotion, and each one his own guardian angel as well. [[5:9|knowing that the same affliction befalls, your brethren who are in the world|Scientes eamdem passionem ei quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitati fieri]], that is, knowing this, that the suffering, tribulation or temptation inflicted on you by enemies visible or invisible is inflicted also on Christians everywhere on earth, that is, on the whole Church: since [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution|omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patiuntur]]. So do not think that something unheard of is happening to you: nay, be ashamed if you are overcome by temptations and tribulations more than others.

paras.t: Circa verba inducta scribit doctor, præsul et martyr gloriosus, S. Cyprianus, qui in Decreto inter doctores catholicos primus exprimitur: Circuit (diabolus) nos singulos, et tanquam hostis clausos obsidens muros, explorat et tentat an sit aliqua pars membrorum minus stabilis et minus fida, cujus aditu ad interiora penetretur. Offert oculis formas illicitas et faciles voluptates, ut visu destruat castitatem; aures per canoram musicam tentat, ut soni dulcioris auditu solvat et emolliat Christiani vigorem; linguam ad convitium provocat; manum, injuriis lacessentibus, ad petulantiam cædis instigat. Ut fraudatorem faciat, lucra opponit injusta; ut animam pecunia capiat, ingerit perniciosa compendia. Honores terrenos promittit, ut cœlestes adimat; ostentat falsa, ut vera subripiat. Et quum latenter non potest fallere, exserte atque aperte minatur, terrorem turbidæ persecutionis intentans. Ad debellandos Dei servos inquietus semper, et semper infestus; in pace subdolus, in persecutione violentus. Quamobrem, fratres dilectissimi, contra omnes diaboli vel fallaces insidias, vel apertas minas, stare debet instructus animus et armatus, tam paratus semper ad repugnandum, quam est ad impugnandum semper paratus inimicus.
paras.en: On the words set down here the glorious doctor, bishop and martyr St. Cyprian, who in the *Decretum* is named first among the catholic doctors, writes: He goes about each of us (the devil), and like an enemy besieging men shut up within walls, he spies out and tries whether there be some part of the members less steadfast and less trustworthy, by entering at which he may make his way into the interior. He presents to the eyes unlawful forms and easy pleasures, to destroy chastity through sight; he tempts the ears with tuneful music, to loosen and soften the Christian's vigour by the hearing of sweeter sound; he provokes the tongue to abuse; he goads the hand, when injuries provoke it, to the wantonness of slaughter. To make a man a cheat, he sets unjust gains before him; to ensnare the soul with money, he thrusts ruinous profits upon it. He promises earthly honours, to take away the heavenly; he displays false things, to steal away the true. And when he cannot deceive secretly, he threatens plainly and openly, holding out the terror of a fierce persecution. Ever restless and ever hostile for the overthrow of the servants of God; crafty in peace, violent in persecution. Wherefore, dearly beloved brethren, against all the devil's deceitful snares or open threats the mind must stand instructed and armed, as ready always to resist as the enemy is always ready to attack.

paras.t: Consequenter princeps Apostolorum animat, firmat, et consolatur eos quibus scripsit, ex spe atque intuitu pietatis divinæ. Deus autem omnis gratiæ, id est, a quo gratia omnis procedit, qui per inspirationem internam, et prædicationem externam, atque miracula, vocavit vos in æternam gloriam suam, id est, ad perpetuam felicitatem vos invitavit, virtuosaque opera, quibus illam promeruistis, vobis largitus est (juxta illud Isaiæ: Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis), in Christo Jesu modicum passos, id est propter Christum et secundum ejus doctrinam pauca perpessos: quia non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis, ad futuram gloriam quæ revelabitur in nobis. Unde et Paulus: Id, inquit, quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ. Siquidem quæcumque et quantumcumque quis patiatur in sæculo isto pro Christo, nullius quasi momenti est respectu eorum quæ pro nobis passus est Filius Dei. Pro quo si quotidie millies moreremur, adhuc permodicum esset, propter incomparabilem dignitatem ipsius, passionisque ejus: quia ut Climacus loquitur, aliud est sanguis Dei, aliud est sanguis servorum. Permodicum quoque est, comparatione æternæ felicitatis: quæ talis ac tanta est, quod pro ea uno die obtinenda, mille annorum labores non essent condigni. Ipse perficiet in vobis quod incepit, confirmabit in via per gratiam, solidabitque in patria per gloriam. Vel: Ipse perficiet intellectum vestrum rationibus credendorum, et purificatæ mentis intelligentia; confirmabit voluntatem per caritatis fervorem, ut neque mors, neque vita poterit vos separare a Deo; solidabitque memoriam, ut fixa et stabilis sit in Deo, nec undique evagetur.
paras.en: Next the prince of the Apostles encourages, strengthens and consoles those to whom he wrote, from the hope and contemplation of the divine goodness. [[5:10|But the God of all grace|Deus autem omnis gratiæ]], that is, He from whom all grace proceeds, [[5:10|who|qui]] by inward inspiration and outward preaching, and by miracles, [[5:10|hath called us unto his eternal glory|vocavit vos in æternam gloriam suam]] [Denis reads *vos*, "you", where the Vulgate has *nos*, "us"], that is, has invited you to perpetual happiness, and has bestowed on you the virtuous works by which you have merited it (according to that word of Isaias: [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis]]), [[5:10|in Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little|in Christo Jesu modicum passos]], that is, having suffered few things for Christ's sake and according to His teaching: for [[Rom 8:18|the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come that shall be revealed in us|non sunt condignæ passiones hujus temporis, ad futuram gloriam quæ revelabitur in nobis]]. Hence Paul too: [[2 Cor 4:17|that|Id]], he says, [[2 Cor 4:17|which is at present momentary and light of our tribulation|quod in præsenti est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ]] [the margin gives I Cor. iv, 17; the words are those of 2 Cor 4:17]. For whatever and however much anyone may suffer in this world for Christ is as of no moment in respect of what the Son of God suffered for us. If we died a thousand times every day for Him, it would still be very little, because of the incomparable dignity of His person and of His passion: for, as Climacus says, the blood of God is one thing, the blood of servants another. It is very little also in comparison with eternal happiness, which is such and so great that the labours of a thousand years would not be worthy of obtaining it for one day. He [[5:10|will himself perfect you|Ipse perficiet]] (that is, perfect in you what He has begun), [[5:10|and confirm you|confirmabit]] on the way by grace, [[5:10|and establish you|solidabitque]] in the fatherland by glory. Or: He will perfect your understanding with the reasons of the things to be believed and with the insight of a purified mind; He will confirm your will through the fervour of charity, so that neither death nor life shall be able to separate you from God; and He will establish your memory, so that it may be fixed and stable in God and not wander off on every side.

paras.t: Ipsi gloria et imperium in sæcula sæculorum. Amen, sicut in præcedenti capitulo est expositum.
paras.en: [[5:11|To him be glory and empire, for ever and ever. Amen|Ipsi gloria et imperium in sæcula sæculorum. Amen]], as has been expounded in the preceding chapter.

paras.t: Deinde Archiapostolus certificat eos quibus scripsit, hanc epistolam vere ab ipso editam ac transmissam. In primitiva namque Ecclesia pseudoapostoli interim sub persona et nomine verorum Apostolorum aliqua conscripserunt et direxerunt. Propter quod ad Thessalonicenses loquitur Paulus: Nemo vos seducat, neque per epistolam, tanquam per nos missam. In fine quoque ad Thessalonicenses epistolæ dicitur: Salutatio mea manu Pauli: quod signum in omni epistola ita scribo. Subditur ergo: Per Silvanum fidelem fratrem vobis, ut arbitror, id est, quem pro vestra salute sollicitum judico seu confido, breviter scripsi vobis, id est, compendiosam istam vobis direxi epistolam: quæ brevis est verbis, sententiis vero diffusa, mirabiliterque præclara.
paras.en: Then the Archapostle assures those to whom he wrote that this epistle was truly composed and sent by him. For in the primitive Church false apostles at times wrote certain things under the person and name of the true Apostles, and sent them. For this reason Paul says to the Thessalonians: [[2 Thess 2:3|Let no man deceive you|Nemo vos seducat]], neither by epistle, [[2 Thess 2:2|as sent from us|tanquam per nos missam]]. At the end of the epistle to the Thessalonians, too, it is said: [[2 Thess 3:17|The salutation of Paul with my own hand: which is the sign in every epistle. So I write.|Salutatio mea manu Pauli: quod signum in omni epistola ita scribo]] There follows, therefore: [[5:12|By Sylvanus, a faithful brother unto you, as I think|Per Silvanum fidelem fratrem vobis, ut arbitror]], that is, one whom I judge or trust to be solicitous for your salvation, [[5:12|I have written briefly|breviter scripsi]] to you, that is, I have sent you this compendious epistle: which is brief in words, but ample in meaning [literally "diffuse in its sentences"], and wonderfully excellent.

paras.t: Quis fuerit iste Silvanus, nec Beda, nec Albertus, nec alius quispiam expositorum quos legi, exprimit in hoc loco. Porro Paulus apostolus in ambabus ad Thessalonicenses epistolis exprimit et annumerat sibi in salutatione Silvanum. Et ibi dicunt expositores, quod ille Silvanus fuerit Silas, de cujus excellentia atque virtutibus multa in Actibus Apostolorum leguntur: quia inter cetera dicitur, quod ipse et Judas, qui cum Paulo et Barnaba ab Apostolis a Jerusalem Antiochiam missi sunt, fuerunt viri primi in fratribus, et prophetæ; deinde, quod Paulus secum assumpsit Silam, qui cum Paulo varias persecutiones perpessus est, et fortiter prædicavit: propter quod meruit apostolus appellari. Itaque, an iste Silvanus fuerit idem ille Silvanus, certum non habeo, præsertim quia (ut asserit Beda et paulo post tangetur) ista epistola scripta et missa est tempore Claudii imperatoris: quo tempore Silam Romæ fuisse non constat. Imo tunc potius videtur fuisse cum Paulo, nisi dicatur ad tempus Romam profectus. Certum est tamen, hunc Silvanum sanctum virum fuisse.
paras.en: Who this Sylvanus was, neither Bede nor Albert nor any other of the expositors I have read states at this place. Now the apostle Paul, in both epistles to the Thessalonians, names Sylvanus and joins him with himself in the salutation. And there the expositors say that that Sylvanus was Silas, of whose excellence and virtues much is read in the Acts of the Apostles: for among other things it is said that he and Judas, who were sent by the Apostles from Jerusalem to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas, were chief men among the brethren, and prophets; and then that Paul took Silas with him, who suffered various persecutions together with Paul and preached boldly: for which he deserved to be called an apostle. And so, whether this Sylvanus was that same Sylvanus I do not hold as certain, especially since (as Bede asserts, and as will be touched on a little later) this epistle was written and sent in the time of the emperor Claudius, at which time it is not established that Silas was at Rome. Rather, he seems then to have been with Paul, unless it be said that he went to Rome for a time. It is certain, however, that this Sylvanus was a holy man.
