paras.t: Itaque, per hunc scripsi, obsecrans, id est, ad observanda quæ scripsi, per sacra vos rogans magis quam jubens. Unde superius: Obsecro, inquit, vos tanquam peregrinos et advenas. Et contestans hanc esse veram gratiam Dei, in qua statis, id est, mente ad Deum erecti estis, ita quod estis vere in caritate et gratia gratum faciente, atque in fide catholica. Quod Deo revelante, princeps Apostolorum cognovit certitudinaliter, aut aliunde per evidentia signa scivit hoc multum probabiliter, vel cognovit illud de eis in generali, quamvis non ita in particulari. Hinc et Paulus eos quibus scripsit, sæpe appellavit sanctos.
paras.en: So by him I have written, [[5:12|beseeching|obsecrans]], that is, begging you by holy things, rather than commanding, to observe what I have written. Hence above: [[2:11|I beseech|Obsecro]], he says, [[2:11|you, as strangers and pilgrims|vos tanquam peregrinos et advenas]]. [[5:12|and testifying that this is the true grace of God, wherein you stand|Et contestans hanc esse veram gratiam Dei, in qua statis]], that is, are raised up in mind to God, so that you are truly in charity and in sanctifying grace [Latin *gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], and in the catholic faith. This the prince of the Apostles knew with certainty by God's revelation, or else knew it with great probability from other, evident signs, or knew it of them in general, though not so in particular. Hence Paul too often called those to whom he wrote saints[[Rom 1:7||]][[1 Cor 1:2||]].

paras.t: Salutat vos Ecclesia, id est, plebs christiana salutem vobis optat, orat et dicit, quæ est in Babylone, id est in Roma, secundum expositores concorditer. Romam quippe nominat Babylonem: Primo, propter nominis interpretationem, quoniam Babylon interpretatur confusio, et in Roma fuit vitiorum omniumque idololatriarum ingens confusio. Omnium enim deorum colebant Romani portenta. Atque, ut asserit Leo Papa, magnam sibi Roma videbatur assumpsisse religionem, quia nullam respuerat falsitatem. Secundo, propter conformitatem ejus cum Babylone. Quemadmodum enim Babylon illa Chaldaica fuit suo tempore urbs possidens monarchiam, et magna valde ac idolis plena, in qua pauca congregatio fuit Israeliticæ plebis, illuc translata: sic Roma tempore conscriptionis hujus epistolæ, fuit metropolis mundi, civitasque monarchica idololatriis plena, in qua adhuc modica fuit Ecclesia. De qua subjungitur: coelecta, vel, ut aliqui textus habent, collecta. Fuit enim instar aliarum Ecclesiarum particularium, simul cum eis Deo electa: quæ et per fidem ac caritatem fuit collecta, unumque in Deo effecta. Et Marcus filius meus. Iste est Marcus evangelista, baptizatus a beatissimo Petro, et instructus ab eo. Ex hoc loco elicit Beda, quod Archiapostolus hanc scripsit epistolam antequam misit Marcum ad Alexandriam, utpote Claudio imperante, sub cujus imperio beatissimus Petrus et Marcus Romam venerunt.
paras.en: [[5:13|The church|Ecclesia]] [[5:13|saluteth you|Salutat vos]], that is, the Christian people wish you salvation, pray for it and say it [the Latin *salutat*, "greets", is from *salus*, "health" or "salvation"], [[5:13|that is in Babylon|quæ est in Babylone]], that is, in Rome, as the expositors agree. For he calls Rome Babylon: first, because of the meaning of the name, since Babylon is interpreted *confusion*, and in Rome there was a vast confusion of vices and of all idolatries. For the Romans worshipped the monstrous figures of all the gods. And, as Pope Leo says, Rome thought she had taken up a great religion, because she had rejected no falsehood. Secondly, because of her likeness to Babylon. For as that Chaldean Babylon was in its time a city holding the monarchy [that is, the empire of the world], very great and full of idols, in which there was a small congregation of the Israelite people, carried away there: so Rome, at the time this epistle was written, was the capital of the world, a monarchical city full of idolatries, in which there was as yet a small Church. Of which it is added: [[5:13|elected together with you|coelecta]], or, as some texts have, *collecta*, gathered together. For it was, like the other particular Churches, elected by God together with them; and it was also gathered together by faith and charity, and made one in God. [[5:13|And so doth my son, Mark|Et Marcus filius meus]]. This is Mark the evangelist, baptized by the most blessed Peter and taught by him. From this place Bede infers that the Archapostle wrote this epistle before he sent Mark to Alexandria, namely in the reign of Claudius, under whose rule the most blessed Peter and Mark came to Rome.

paras.t: Salutate invicem in osculo sancto. Hoc in suis epistolis sæpe scripsit et Paulus. Fuit siquidem in primitiva Ecclesia, caritate adhuc abundante ac superfluente, consuetudo, quod fideles se invicem cum osculo receperunt ac salutaverunt, quia et Christus suos discipulos sic osculari solitus fuit. Unde et proditor: Quemcumque, inquit, osculatus fuero, ipse est. Itaque, Salutate in osculo sancto, spirituali, caritativo, pacifico; non carnali, blando, fallaci, iniquo, quemadmodum Joab osculatus est Amasam, proditor Salvatorem, Salomon alienigenas mulieres. Quidam vero sub specie osculi spiritualis, suam palliant carnalitatem, et osculo utuntur carnali: quod prorsus cavendum est.
paras.en: [[5:14|Salute one another with a holy kiss|Salutate invicem in osculo sancto]]. This Paul too often wrote in his epistles[[Rom 16:16||]][[1 Cor 16:20||]][[2 Cor 13:12||]][[1 Thess 5:26||]]. For in the primitive Church, while charity still abounded and overflowed, it was the custom for the faithful to receive and greet one another with a kiss, because Christ too was wont to kiss His disciples so. Hence the traitor too: [[Matt 26:48|Whomsoever|Quemcumque]], he says, [[Matt 26:48|I shall kiss, that is he|osculatus fuero, ipse est]]. So, [[5:14|Salute|Salutate]] [[5:14|with a holy kiss|in osculo sancto]], a spiritual, charitable, peaceable one; not with a carnal, flattering, deceitful, wicked one, as Joab kissed Amasa[[2 Kings 20:9||]], the traitor the Saviour[[Matt 26:49||]], Solomon the strange women[[3 Kings 11:1||]][[3 Kings 11:2||]]. Some, however, under the appearance of a spiritual kiss, cloak their carnality and use a carnal kiss: which is to be wholly avoided.

paras.t: Gratia vobis omnibus sit, qui estis in Christo Jesu, id est, ei per fidem et caritatem estis uniti et incorporati, quemadmodum ipse Joannes fatetur: Omnes unum sint, sicut tu, Pater, in me, et ego in te, ut et ipsi in nobis unum sint. Sed quum isti essent in gratia, sicut jam paulo superius dixit, Contestans hanc esse veram gratiam in qua statis: cur eis nunc gratiam imprecatur? Sed respondendum, quod gratiam communicantem et consummantem eis exoptat, atque assiduum divinorum charismatum incrementum. Ad laudem et gloriam Omnipotentis, qui est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[5:14|Grace be to all you|Gratia vobis omnibus]], [[5:14|who are in Christ Jesus|qui estis in Christo Jesu]], that is, who are united to Him and incorporated in Him by faith and charity, as John himself declares: [[John 17:21|That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee; that they also may be one in us|Omnes unum sint, sicut tu, Pater, in me, et ego in te, ut et ipsi in nobis unum sint]]. But since these were in grace, as he said a little above, [[5:12|testifying that this is the true grace of God, wherein you stand|Contestans hanc esse veram gratiam in qua statis]], why does he now pray for grace for them? The answer must be that he desires for them grace imparted and brought to completion [Latin *gratiam communicantem et consummantem*], and a constant increase of the divine gifts. To the praise and glory of the Almighty, who is God exalted above all things and blessed. Amen.
